records.qtitle: Funds to athletes under the TOP Scheme
records.name: Renuka Chowdhury
records.qn_text: (a) whether Government has recently revised the guidelines for issuance of funds to athletes under the Target Olympic Podium (TOP) Scheme;<br/><br/>(b) if so, the details thereof; and<br/><br/>(c) the fresh steps taken by Government to curb red-tapism as well as misuse of funds by athletes<br/>under the TOP Scheme?
records.ans_text: THE MINISTER OF STATE (INDEPENDENT CHARGE)<br/>FOR YOUTH AFFAIRS AND SPORTS<br/>[COL. RAJYAVARDHAN RATHORE (RETD.)]<br/><br/>(a) to (c): A Statement is laid on the table of the House.<br/>STATEMENT REFERED TO IN REPLY TO PARTS (A) TO (C) OF STARRED QUESTION NO.353 TO BE ANSWERED ON 28-03-2018 BY SHRIMATI RENUKA CHOWDHURY REGARDING FUNDS TO ATHLETES UNDER THE TOP SCHEME.<br/><br/>(a) & (b): Sir, Selection of athletes for inclusion in Target Olympic Podium (TOP) Scheme was being done on the basis of recommendations of Target Olympic Podium (TOP) Elite Identification Committee, the proposals of athletes for inclusion in TOP Scheme are now being<br/>considered by the designated committee in the Mission Olympic Cell (MOC) headed by Director<br/>General, Sports Authority of India (SAI). The designated committee in MOC can ask the existing members of TOP Elite Identification Committee to attend the meetings.<br/><br/>There is no change in the overall procedure in providing financial support to the Athletes<br/>selected under Target Olympic Podium (TOP) Scheme. The MOC takes a holistic view of the<br/>requirements of the Athletes and approves financial support. Funds, upto 90% of the approved<br/>amount of assistance, are released to the Athletes and/or the Training Institutes; balance amount<br/>is released after completion of training and submission of necessary documents, which include<br/>report of the Institute/Coach on performance/training of the athletes and statement of accounts.<br/>The Athletes under TOPS are also given ‘Out of Pocket Allowance’ at the rate of Rs.50,000.00<br/>per month, which is released directly to the accounts of concerned athletes.<br/><br/>(c): Procedure listed in reply to parts (a) & (b) above simplifies the processing of proposals<br/>and ensures expeditious release of funds to athletes.<br/><br/>To ensure that funds are properly utilized by the athletes, report from training institutes<br/>are sought and examined. Accounts on training expenses submitted by athletes are also verified<br/>and examined.<br/>****

records.qtitle: Payment of enhanced wages
records.name: Renuka Chowdhury
records.qn_text: (a)whether Government had increased minimum wages for workers engaged in sweeping and cleaning activities by 40 per cent w.e.f. 19th January, 2017;<br/>(b)if so, the reasons for not implementing the notification by the contractors engaged by Central Government offices and agencies particularly the Indian Railways; and<br/>(c)the steps taken by Government for proper implementation of the notification and to ensure payment of wages at enhanced rates to workers engaged in sweeping and cleaning activities?<br/>
records.ans_text: MINISTER OF STATE(IC) FOR LABOUR AND EMPLOYMENT<br/>(SHRI SANTOSH KUMAR GANGWAR)<br/><br/>(a):	 Yes, Sir. The Government had increased the basic rate of minimum wages for sweeping and cleaning activities in the central sphere through the notification w.e.f. 19.01.2017. Minimum Wage (per day) for sweeping and cleaning worker were increased by more than 40 percent from Rs. 250/- to Rs. 350/- in the ‘C’ Area category; Rs. 312/- to Rs. 437/- in ‘B’ Area category and Rs. 374/- to Rs. 523/- in ‘A’ Area category.<br/>Contd..2/-<br/><br/>::   2  ::<br/>(b):	 This Ministry is in constant endeavor towards implementing the revised rates of minimum wages. As far as employees in Railway are concerned guidelines were issued to Ministry of Railways/Railway Board. Ministry of Railways has also issued instructions to its Zonal Offices across the country for strict compliance of minimum wages. The data regarding implementation of Minimum Wages Act for the last one year is enclosed as Annexure ’A’.<br/><br/>(c):	 The Minimum Wages Act, 1948 is implemented by the Centre as well as the States in respect of their respective jurisdiction. In the Central Sphere, the enforcement is secured through the Inspecting Officers of the Chief Labour Commissioner (Central) commonly designated as Central Industrial Relations Machinery (CIRM), the compliance in the State sphere is ensured through the State Enforcement Machinery. They conduct regular inspections and in the event of detection of any case of non-payment or under-payment of minimum wages, they advise the employers to make payment of the shortfall of wages. In case of non-compliance, penal provisions against the defaulting employers are invoked.   <br/>*                                                           ******<br/>

records.qtitle: Student Police Cadet Programme
records.name: Renuka Chowdhury
records.qn_text: (a) whether Government proposes to launch a Student Police Cadet (SPC) Programme across the country; <br/><br/>(b) if so, the salient features of the programme; and <br/><br/>(c) the steps taken by Government to encourage students to understand the importance of rule of law and its role in peace, development and sustained creation of new income and employment opportunities?
records.ans_text: MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HOME AFFAIRS<br/>(SHRI HANSRAJ GANGARAM AHIR)<br/><br/>(a):	Yes Sir.<br/><br/>(b) & (c):	The SPC programme aims to impart values to school-going students to enable them to become responsible citizen. The programme intends to introduce a robust interface mechanism between police and students to achieve public safety in the society. The programme will lay the foundation for harmonious relationship between the police and the society, at large, for peace and social order. <br/><br/>The Bureau of Police Research & Development (BPR&D) has developed a National Model Syllabus for the SPC programme. BPR&D has also identified more than 30 other topics that can be taught to students of class 8th& 9th standard in various schools of the Country.<br/><br/><br/><br/> <br/>                         ***********

records.qtitle: Guidelines for safe disposal of expired medicines
records.name: Renuka Chowdhury
records.qn_text: Will the Minister of HEALTH AND FAMILY WELFARE be pleased to state:<br/><br/>(a) whether Government has formulated any clear guidelines for safe disposal of expired and leftover antibiotics;<br/><br/>(b) if so, the details thereof and if not, the reasons therefor; and<br/><br/>(c) the fresh steps taken by Government to check growing anti-microbial resistance due to discharge of drugs and chemicals into environment?<br/><br/>
records.ans_text: ANSWER<br/>THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HEALTH AND <br/>FAMILY WELFARE<br/>(SHRI ASHWINI KUMAR CHOUBEY)<br/>(a) to (c):	Good Manufacturing Practices (GMP) and Requirements of Premises, Plant and Equipment for pharmaceutical products laid down in   Schedule M of the Drugs and Cosmetics Rules, 1945 prescribe the requirements for disposal of waste including the rejected drugs. Details are as under:<br/>I.	The disposal of sewage and effluents (solid, liquid and gas) from the manufactory shall be in conformity with the requirements of Environment Pollution Control Board.<br/>II.	 All bio-medical waste shall be destroyed as per the provisions of the Bio-Medical Waste (Management and Handling) Rules, 1996. <br/>III.	 Additional precautions shall be taken for the storage and disposal of rejected drugs. Records shall be maintained for all disposal of waste.<br/>IV.	Provisions shall be made for the proper and safe storage of waste materials awaiting disposal. Hazardous, toxic substances and flammable materials shall be stored in suitably designed and segregated, enclosed areas in conformity with Central and State Legislations.<br/><br/>One of the conditions of drug manufacturing license granted under the Drugs and Cosmetics Rules, 1940 is that the Licensees shall comply with the Good Manufacturing Practices (GMP) requirements prescribed in   Schedule M of the said Rules. State Licensing Authorities appointed by the respective State Governments are empowered to take action in case of any violation of above requirements.<br/><br/>       The Government has taken various regulatory measures to curb the misuse of antibiotics. However, no report/incidence of growing of anti-microbial resistance of drugs due to discharge of drugs and chemicals into environment has been brought to notice of this Ministry.<br/>

records.qtitle: Non accreditation with NABH by hospitals
records.name: Renuka Chowdhury
records.qn_text: Will the Minister of HEALTH AND FAMILY WELFARE be pleased to state: <br/><br/>(a) whether it is a fact that only one per cent of all the hospitals/nursing homes in the Country have applied for NABH (National Accreditation Board for Hospitals) accreditation even after 12 years of its establishment; <br/><br/>(b) if so, the reasons for such reluctant attitude of hospitals and nursing homes; and <br/><br/>(c) the fresh steps taken by Government to ensure availability of best quality health services in the country?<br/>
records.ans_text: ANSWER<br/>THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HEALTH AND <br/>FAMILY WELFARE<br/>(SMT. ANUPRIYA PATEL)<br/> (a)& (b):    As per the information made available by Quality Council of India, it is difficult to state the exact percentage of the hospitals/nursing homes in the country that have applied for NABH (National Accreditation Board for Hospitals) accreditation as there is no exact count of all the hospitals and nursing homes in the country. Current accredited healthcare organizations are over 2000.<br/>NABH Accreditation is a voluntary process and therefore it is entirely up to the healthcare organization whether to adopt it or not.<br/>(c):       Health is a State subject. The Government of India has, however, enacted the Clinical Establishments (Registration and Regulation) Act, 2010 and notified Clinical Establishments (Central Government) Rules, 2012. These provide for registration and regulation of Clinical Establishments including those in the private sector. The Act is currently applicable in eleven States and all Union Territories except Delhi. Other States may adopt the Act under clause (1) of Article 252 of the Constitution. <br/>In accordance with the Clinical Establishments (Central Government) Rules, 2012 under the aforementioned Act, in the States/Union Territories where the said Act is in force, the clinical establishments are required to meet the norms such as minimum standards of facilities and services, minimum requirement of personnel, maintenance of records and reports  and displaying of rates at a conspicuous place. The clinical establishments are also required to follow Standard Treatment Guidelines issued by the Central/State Governments and charge rates for each type of procedure and service within the range of rates determined from time to time in consultation with the State Governments. The implementation and enforcement of the said Act falls within the ambit of the States/Union territories.<br/>………………….<br/>

records.ans_text: The Minister of State in the Ministry of CIVIL AVIATION      (Shri Jayant Sinha)<br/><br/>(a) & (b) : There is no such proposal with the Govt. of India. However, Commercial Air Transport Service Providers, with the permission of the State Government and by following the approval process, as required under relevant Civil Aviation Requirement (CAR), may operate from any waterdrome approved for the purpose, anywhere in the Country.<br/><br/>  <br/>(c) : Seaplane services can be operated under Scheduled / Non-Scheduled Air Transport Services by complying with the requirement as contained in CAR Section 3 Series C Part XII and CAR Section 3 Series C Part III. The operational and Airworthiness requirements for operation of Seaplane Services are available in CAR Section 3 Series C Part IX.<br/>

records.qtitle: NHAI bonds for highway projects

records.qn_text: (a) 	whether the National Highways Authority of India (NHAI) plans to issue bonds to finance highway projects;<br/><br/>(b)	 if so, the details of the proposal; and <br/><br/>(c) 	the steps taken by Government to generate funds from various portfolios by adopting proactive infrastructural policies?<br/>
records.ans_text: THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF ROAD TRANSPORT AND HIGHWAYS<br/><br/>(SHRI MANSUKH L. MANDAVIYA)<br/><br/><br/>(a)&(b) Yes, Sir.  NHAI has been mandated to raise funds aggregating to Rs. 59,270 crore during the current financial year.  NHAI has raised   Rs. 28,893 crore through various types of bonds and Rs. 20,000 crore  raised as loan from NSSF collection totaling to Rs. 48,893 Crore till February 2018.   Further, the IEBR (Internal & Extra Budgetary Resources) amount approved for 2018-19 is Rs. 62,000 Crore, which will be raised via bonds like Bharatmala Bonds, Masala Bonds, 54 EC Capital Gain Bonds, taxable bonds and from institutions like LIC, EPFO and NSSF collection etc.<br/> <br/>(c)	TOT model is a proactive infrastructural policy of the Government to     generate funds for road sector.<br/>

records.qtitle: CPCSEA registration of Universities
records.name: Renuka Chowdhury
records.qn_text: (a) whether a large number of universities which are running courses in Life Science and Zoology, are not registered with the Committee for the purpose of Control and Supervision of Experiments on Animals (CPCSEA);<br/><br/>(b) if so, the details thereof along with the reasons therefor; and  <br/><br/>(c)  the steps taken by Government to ensure that all the establishments having facilities for animal dissection are registered with CPCSEA?<br/>
records.ans_text: MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF ENVIRONMENT, FOREST AND CLIMATE CHANGE  (DR. MAHESH SHARMA)<br/><br/>(a) & (b)The dissection and experimentation of animals in undergraduate and post graduate courses of Zoology and Life Sciences is banned by UGC. The Colleges/Universities conducting Life Science Courses and conducting experiments on laboratory animals are registered with CPCSEA. <br/><br/>(c) The CPCSEA has been writing to UGC, MCI, PCI, and AICTE since May 2014 onwards for getting the establishments, coming under the purview of the above respective councils and conducting experiments on laboratory animals, to get registered with CPCSEA. A Public Notice was also published in the leading national dailies for awareness regarding registration with CPCSEA before conducting experiment/breeding/trading of laboratory animals. Further, letters have also been written to the nominees of CPCSEA and to the registrar of companies for asking the unregistered establishments conducting experiments on animals to get registered with CPCSEA. Funding agencies like DBT, DST, ICAR, ICMR and CSIR have also been requested to not extend financial assistance to those who are conducting research on animals without being registered with CPCSEA. Unregistered establishments which are found to be conducting animal related work are asked to immediately stop their work till the time they get registered with CPCSEA.<br/>

records.qtitle: Station Development Plan for Secunderabad and Vijayawada railway stations
records.name: Renuka Chowdhury
records.qn_text: (a)     whether Railways have decided for re-development of a number of stations under the first phase of Station Development Plan;<br/><br/>(b)	if so, the reasons for delay in execution of the Station Development Plan in respect of Secunderabad and Vijayawada railway stations under South Central Railway; and<br/>(c)	   the fresh steps taken by Government for time- bound execution of all the phases of Station Development Plan?<br/><br/>
records.ans_text: MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF RAILWAYS<br/><br/>(SHRI RAJEN GOHAIN)<br/><br/>(a) & (b):  Yes, Sir. 23 stations (including Secunderabad and Vijayawada) were taken up for bidding in first phase by Zonal Railways under Station Redevelopment Program. Out of these 23 stations, bids were received for Jammu Tawi and Kozhikode stations only, which are under evaluation. No bids were received for other stations. In view of the not so-encouraging response, bids for these stations were foreclosed.<br/>(c):  At present, Ministry of Railways is formulating revised schemes for station redevelopment on fast track. The proposals for redevelopment of more stations will be taken up, once the revised strategy for redevelopment of stations is finalised.<br/><br/><br/>*****<br/><br/>

records.qtitle: Disposal of consumers grievances
records.name: Renuka Chowdhury
records.min_name: CONSUMER AFFAIRS, FOOD AND PUBLIC DISTRIBUTION
records.qn_text: (a) 	whether Government proposes to constitute a Central Consumer Protection Authority; (b) 	if so, the details thereof along with its terms of reference; and <br/>(c)	the fresh steps taken by Government to ensure that consumers’ grievances are redressed in a time-bound manner at least possible cost?<br/>
records.ans_text: THE MINISTER OF <br/>CONSUMER AFFAIRS, FOOD AND PUBLIC DISTRIBUTION<br/>(SHRI RAM VILAS PASWAN)<br/><br/>(a) & (b) : Yes, Sir. The Department of Consumer Affairs introduced the Consumer Protection Bill, 2018 in the Lok Sabha on 5.1.2018.  The Bill seeks to provide for establishment of an executive agency to be called the Central Consumer Protection Authority (CCPA) to regulate matters relating to violation of rights of consumers, unfair trade practices,   false or misleading advertisements and also to promote, protect and enforce the rights of consumers as a class.<br/>(c)          :  In addition to making the three-tier quasi-judicial system ( District Consumer Disputes Redressal Forum, State Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission and the National Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission) set up under the provisions of the Consumer Protection Act, 1986, more efficient, the National Consumer Helpline, established by the Department as an alternate grievance redressal mechanism, has been strengthened by way of launching an Integrated Grievance Redressal Mechanism ( INGRAM) portal, increasing of helpdesks from 14 to 60.  Also, six Zonal Consumer Helplines have been set up with ten help desks each at Ahmedabad, Bengaluru, Guwahati, Jaipur, Kolkata and Patna to attend grievances in regional languages.  To fast track resolution of consumer grievances around four hundred companies have been brought under the convergence programme of the National Consumer Helpline.<br/>*****<br/>

records.qtitle: Revial of Ramagundam fertilizer unit
records.name: Renuka Chowdhury
records.qn_text: Will the Minister of CHEMICALS AND FERTILIZERS be pleased to state:<br/><br/><br/>(a) 	whether Government had planned revival of Ramagundam fertilizer unit of Fertilizer Corporation of India Limited by 2018;<br/><br/>(b)	if so, the present status of the work along with the reasons for the delay; and<br/><br/>(c) 	the steps taken by Government for revival of the plant in a time- bound 	manner<br/>
records.ans_text: MINISTER OF STATE (INDEPENDENT CHARGE) FOR THE MINISTRY OF PLANNING; AND MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF CHEMICALS & FERTILIZERS<br/><br/>                                      (RAO INDERJIT SINGH)<br/><br/>(a): 	Yes Sir, the Government has planned revival of Ramagundam Fertilizer unit  of Fertilizer Corporation of India Limited by 2018.<br/><br/>(b) to (c):    At present, the construction activity at project site is in full swing and it has crossed the stage of 77.3% overall progress as on 15.03.2018. Some of the challenges include the following: -<br/><br/>(i)	Ensuring availability of Natural Gas by July, 2018. <br/><br/>(ii)	Ensuring availability of water from Yellampalli Barrage through 28 KM long pipeline by April, 2018.<br/><br/>(iii)	and timely completion of the water package, Power Plant etc.<br/><br/>	Department of Fertilizers (DoF) has taken up the matter with State Government of Telangana for laying of water pipeline and power grid connectivity within April, 2018.  DoF  has also taken up the matter with M/s GITL (GSPL India Transco Limited) for completion of gas pipeline within July, 2018.<br/><br/>	In parallel, an aggressive follow – up with M/s Bharat Heavy Electricals Ltd. (BHEL), WIPRO and other contractors deployed at site is also being undertaken by Executive Management of Ramagundam and Fertilizer Chemicals Limited (RFCL) on regular basis.<br/><br/><br/>                            ********<br/>

records.qtitle: Status of PMMVY
records.name: Renuka Chowdhury
records.qn_text: (a)	the present status of implementation of Pradhan Mantri Matru Vandana Yojana (PMMVY);<br/><br/>(b)	the total funds allocated vis-a-vis disbursed to beneficiaries under the scheme during the last two years; and<br/><br/>(c)	the steps taken by Government to provide benefits of the scheme to all pregnant and lactating mothers irrespective of number of children? <br/>
records.ans_text: MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF  WOMEN AND CHILD DEVELOPMENT<br/>(DR. VIRENDRA KUMAR)<br/><br/>(a)	The Government has approved Pan-India implementation of Pradhan Mantri Matru Vandana Yojana (PMMVY) on 17.05.2017 for implementation across the country with effect from 01.01.2017. The implementation guidelines of the scheme and Pradhan Mantri Matru Vandana Yojana-Common Application Software (PMMVY-CAS) has been launched on 01.09.2017. So far, more than 18.31 lakhs beneficiaries have been enrolled for receiving maternity benefit on web-based dedicated MIS software PMMVY-CAS. <br/><br/>(b)	The Budget Estimates (BE) for the financial year 2017-18 is ? 2700.00 crores which has been reduced to ? 2594.55 crores at Revised Estimates (RE) stage. Out of ? 2594.55 crores, Ministry has sanctioned/released ? 2048.92 crores to all 36 States/UTs. Maternity benefits amounting to more than ? 180.00 crores have been disbursed to approximately 8 lakh beneficiaries by 29 States/UTs under the scheme as on 18.03.2018. <br/><br/>(c)	No such proposal is under consideration of the Ministry.<br/><br/>*******<br/>

records.qtitle: Setting up of NIMHR
records.name: Renuka Chowdhury
records.qn_text: (a) whether Government had proposed in 2014 to set up a National Institute of Mental Health Rehabilitation (NIMHR);<br/>(b) if so, the present status of work on the proposal;<br/>(c) the number of people treated for mental illness and became fit to rejoin society, at present; and<br/>(d) the fresh steps taken by Government for a time-bound execution of work on the project?<br/>
records.ans_text: (a)	Yes, Sir.<br/><br/>(b) to (d) The Ministry has firmed up a proposal to establish the National Institute of Mental Health Rehabilitation at Bhopal, Madhya Pradesh, and the same has been considered and recommended by the Expenditure Finance Committee. The Ministry has circulated a Cabinet note for consideration of the establishment of the proposed institute on 13.03.2018.        <br/>As regards the number of people treated for mental illness, Ministry of Health & Family Welfare have informed that the data regarding number of persons who became fit to rejoin society after being treated for mental illness is not maintained centrally by them.<br/><br/><br/>

records.qtitle: Implementation of UGC Grievances Redressal Regulations
records.name: Renuka Chowdhury
records.qn_text: (a) whether certain universities in the country have not yet implemented the UGC Grievance Redressal Regulations, 2012;<br/>(b) if so, the details thereof along with the reasons therefor; and <br/>(c) the steps taken by Government for mandatory appointment of ombudsman in each university for redressal of grievances of students?
records.ans_text: MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HUMAN RESOURCE DEVELOPMENT<br/>(DR. SATYA PAL SINGH)<br/><br/>(a) to (c): The University Grants Commission (UGC) Grievance Redressal Regulations, 2012 prescribes for well defined systems and procedures for redressal of grievances of aggrieved students in Universities and Colleges. These regulations are mandatory for implementation by all Universities/affiliated Colleges in India. UGC issues directions to Universities, from time to time, to effectively implement grievance redressal regulations. Further, as per these regulations, an Ombudsman is required to be appointed by each university to effectively address and resolve grievances lodged by students at University level. The UGC has been closely monitoring the implementation of the grievance redressal systems and procedures as contained in the Regulations.<br/><br/>	The UGC has launched an Online Student Grievance Redressal Portal to ensure transparency in admission, prevent unfair practices in Higher Education Institutions and provide effective mechanism for redressal of the grievances. This Portal facilitates the students/complainants to lodge their grievance, send reminders and view the status of action taken on their grievances. The system also facilitates Universities to search and browse grievances lodged by the students and post action taken on complaints as well as contact complainant directly through e-mail, phone or by post. <br/>******

records.qtitle: Transparency in selection of deserving players under Khelo India

records.ans_text: THE MINISTER OF STATE (INDEPENDENT CHARGE)<br/>FOR YOUTH AFFAIRS & SPORTS<br/>{COL. RAJYAVARDHAN RATHORE (RETD.)}<br/><br/>(a) The process of talent identification under the Khelo India Scheme has started and about 1000 children are proposed to be included in the scholarship program in the first year. Details of players identified/selected so far under the Khelo India Scheme, sports discipline-wise and State-wise are given in Annexure – I. Process of further scrutinizing these names is under process.<br/>(b) & (c) Identification of talented sportspersons through various avenues and nurturing of such identified sporting talents through a Long Term Athlete Development Programme (LTAD) is done through a detailed and transparent procedure entailing selection through a three-tier structure. Thus, all sportspersons who meet the detailed criteria defined under the guidelines are selected for support. A brief on the procedure adopted for the purpose as per guidelines framed under this vertical of the Khelo India Scheme is given in Annexure – II. Complaints received are also being examined in a transparent manner and proper action is being taken.<br/>*****

records.qtitle: Setting up of IISD
records.name: Renuka Chowdhury
records.qn_text: (a) 	whether Government proposes to set up an Indian Institute of Skill Development (IISD) in every State;<br/><br/>(b)	if so, the details thereof; and<br/>(c)	the  steps  taken  by  Government  to take  up  certification  of  passion-driven skills of those like carpenters, ironsmiths, masons and agriculturists among others to augment  their  livelihood  opportunities  as well  as  to  enable  them  to  become entrepreneurs?<br/>
records.ans_text: (a) & (b) 	Indian Institutes of Skills (IISs) are being established in the country to enhance training standards beyond the current programmes available in the skill eco-system and to provide ‘hands on skills’ training to trainees in specialised areas in collaboration with industry catering to local/ regional industry requirements. Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship has requested all State Governments to look into feasibility of making available land in setting up of IISs in different states.<br/><br/>(c) 	Pradhan Mantri Kaushal Vikas Yojana (PMKVY) is the flagship skill development scheme of Government of India targeting to skill youth from all sections of the society. PMKVY, implemented through National Skill Development Corporation (NSDC), enables youth for taking Short Term Training (STT) and Recognition of Prior Learning (RPL) through accredited and affiliated training provider/training centers. Under RPL, individuals with prior learning experience or skills are assessed and certified. RPL mainly focuses on the individuals engaged in unregulated/informal sectors.<br/>

records.qtitle: Major reforms in MBBS curriculum
records.name: Renuka Chowdhury
records.qn_text: Will the Minister of HEALTH AND FAMILY WELFARE be pleased to state:<br/><br/>(a) whether Government proposes major reforms in MBBS curriculum;<br/><br/>(b) if so, the salient features thereof; and<br/><br/>(c) the time by which new curriculum is likely to be ready for medical students?<br/>
records.ans_text: ANSWER<br/>THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HEALTH AND <br/>FAMILY WELFARE<br/>(SHRI ASHWINI KUMAR CHOUBEY)<br/>(a) to (c):	Medical Council of India (MCI) is a statutory body to prescribe and maintain standards in medical education in the country. The curriculum for MBBS course is prescribed under the Graduate Medical Education Regulations, 1997. The Reconciliation Board of MCI has revised the MBBS curriculum to make it competency based at par with global standards. It was done in consultation with all the stakeholders including inviting comments from the public. The proposal of MCI was examined by a technical committee in the Directorate General of Health Services, Ministry of Health and Family Welfare (MoHFW) and approval with certain observations has been conveyed to MCI. It is now proposed that the undergraduate programme would include a foundation course of one month to orient students to medical profession, ethics, patient safety, national health priorities, alternate health systems etc. The students would be provided early clinical exposure and enhancement of professional development including attitude, ethics and communication skills. As per the information provided by MCI, the new curriculum has been copyrighted.<br/><br/><br/><br/><br/><br/>

records.ans_text: THE MINISTER OF STATE FOR WATER RESOURCES, RIVER DEVELOPMENT AND GANGA REJUVENATION & HUMAN RESOURCES DEVELOPMENT<br/><br/>(DR. SATYA PAL SINGH)<br/><br/>(a) to (c) Maily se Nirmal Yamuna revitalization Project is being implemented in two phases, details of which are provided below: <br/><br/>Phase-I: Under this phase, 14 decentralised Sewage Treatment Plants (STPs) are to be constructed in command area of Najafgarh drain (Dhansa to Keshopur) in Delhi. Shahdara Outfall drain, Qudsia Bagh + Mori Gate drain, Barapula drain, Maharani Bagh drain, Kalkaji drain and Tehkhand Nala has been undertaken at a total cost of Rs. 1062 crore.  <br/>		<br/>NMCG has been taking up regular monitoring of the project and periodical discussions are held with the State agencies to ensure result oriented and expeditious implementation of the project.<br/><br/>******<br/>

records.qtitle: Policy for contract farming
records.name: Renuka Chowdhury
records.qn_text: (a) 	whether Government has formulated any regulatory and policy framework for contract farming;<br/><br/>(b) 	if so, the details thereof; and<br/><br/>(c) 	the fresh steps taken by Government to integrate farmers with agro-industries so as to ensure better price realization for their produces?<br/>
records.ans_text: MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF AGRICULTURE AND FARMERS WELFARE<br/><br/>( SHRI GAJENDRA SINGH SHEKHAWAT)  <br/><br/>(a) & (b):	Yes Sir.  The Government is formulating a progressive, holistic and facilitative model Contract Farming Act with provisions for  integrating food processors with farmers with an aim to ensure better price realization to the farmers for their produce besides reducing post-harvest losses and incentivizing the private sector processors to invest in processing activities. <br/><br/>Comments of various stakeholders have been solicited on the draft model Contract Farming Act including placing it on the website inviting comments of the public.<br/><br/>(c):	The Government through Pradhan Mantri Kisan SAMPADA Yojana (Scheme for Agro-Marine Processing and Development of Agro-Processing Clusters), Mission for Integrated Development of Horticulture (MIDH), Agriculture Marketing Infrastructure (AMI) schemes, is integrating farmers with Agro Industries. Further, the adoption of model Contract Farming Act by States will also ensure integration of farmers with agro-industries so as to ensure better price realization for their produce.<br/><br/><br/><br/>*****<br/>

records.qtitle: Abolition of Devdasi System
records.name: Renuka Chowdhury
records.qn_text: (a)	whether Government is aware of continuance of inhuman treatment of girls and women in the name of Devdasi System in Tiruvallur, Tamil Nadu and Chittoor in Andhra Pradesh at present; <br/><br/>(b)	if so, the reasons why the Devdasi system is still in existence despite ban; and <br/><br/>(c) 		   the steps taken by Government to abolish this heinous practice?<br/>
records.ans_text: <br/>MINISTER OF STATE OF MINISTRY OF WOMEN AND CHILD DEVELOPMENT<br/>(DR. VIRENDRA KUMAR)<br/><br/>(a) 	to (c):  Devdasi System has been prevailing in Andhra Pradesh, Maharashtra and Karnataka. The States of Andhra Pradesh, Maharashtra and Karnataka already have Acts on provision and dedication of Devdasis. Under these Acts whoever performs, promotes, abets, takes part in dedication ceremony is liable for punishment. Further ‘Police’ and ‘Public Order’ are State subjects under the Seventh Schedule to the Constitution of India. The responsibility to maintain law and order protection of life and property of the citizens rests primarily with the respective State Governments. The State Governments are competent to deal with such offences under the extant provisions of laws. Ministry of Home Affaris has issued an advisory dated 22nd December, 2015 regarding “Abolition of Devdasi System”. The advisory is available at www.mha.nic.in.  <br/><br/>****<br/>

records.qtitle: Steps taken to prevent custodial cruelty
records.name: Renuka Chowdhury
records.qn_text: (a) whether Government proposes to ratify the 1997 United Nations convention against torture in custody;<br/><br/>(b) if so, the details thereof and if not, the reasons therefor; and<br/><br/>(c) the steps taken by Government to prevent custodial cruelty and also to punish<br/>its perpetrators?
records.ans_text: MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HOME AFFAIRS<br/>(SHRI HANSRAJ GANGARAM AHIR)<br/><br/>(a)	& (b): The proposed amendments to sections 330 & 331 of Indian Penal Code to define the words “Torture” and “Public Servant” were included in the Criminal Law (Amendment) Bill, 2016, and the draft formulation was circulated to all the State Governments/UTs. The proposal was also forwarded to Law Commission of India for their comments. The Law Commission, after examining this Ministry’s draft formulation, has submitted its 273rd Report on “Implementation of United Nations Convention against Torture and other Cruel, Inhuman and Degrading Treatment or Punishment” on 30.10.2017 along with a draft “The Prevention of Torture Bill, 2017.” As Criminal Laws are in the Concurrent List, this Report along with the draft Bill has been circulated to the State Governments/UTs for their views. <br/><br/>(c) Police and Public Order are State subjects and the State Governments are primarily responsible for enforcing the law to prevent custodial cruelty and also to punish its perpetrators.   <br/><br/><br/><br/><br/>                            *********

records.qtitle: Monthly financial assistance to TB patients
records.name: Renuka Chowdhury
records.qn_text: Will the Minister of HEALTH AND FAMILY WELFARE be pleased to state: <br/><br/>(a) whether Government has decided to provide monthly financial assistance to TB patients across the country; <br/><br/>(b) if so, the details thereof; and <br/><br/>(c) the fresh steps taken by Government to improve the nutritional status of TB patients in the country?<br/>
records.ans_text: ANSWER<br/>THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HEALTH AND <br/>FAMILY WELFARE<br/>(SMT. ANUPRIYA PATEL)<br/>(a) to (c) Yes, under the Revised National Tuberculosis Control Programme (RNTCP), Government has proposed an incentive of  Rs.500 per patient per month for the nutritional support of the TB-affected patients during the course of the treatment. The States have the option for providing these incentives in cash or kind.<br/>The Ministry has formulated the Guidance Document on nutritional care and support for TB patients which includes guidance on nutritional assessment, counselling and appropriate dietary advice.  The programme is also facilitating the TB patients to avail various social support schemes of the State Governments.<br/>………………..<br/>

records.qtitle: Separate window for Islamic banking
records.name: Renuka Chowdhury
records.qn_text: (a)	whether the Reserve Bank of India has ruled out the proposal of opening of a separate window in banks on the principles of Islamic Banking;  <br/><br/>(b)	if so, the reasons for which the Federal Bank has been allowed to launch a non-interest banking savings account viz. “Noor Personal Account” based on Islamic Banking; and<br/><br/>(c)	the corrective steps taken by Government in this regard?<br/> <br/>
records.ans_text: The Minister of State in the Ministry of Finance<br/><br/>(a): Reserve Bank of India (RBI) had suggested that a few products may be considered for introduction through Islamic window of banks after notification. Considering, inter alia, legal challenges involved in introducing Islamic banking products, it was decided not to pursue the matter.<br/><br/>(b) and (c): RBI has informed that it has not allowed Federal Bank to launch any non-interest bearing savings account and that Federal Bank had informed that “Noor Personal Account” is not a savings account, but a variant of current account scheme designed for individuals. <br/>*******<br/>

records.qtitle: Relief and rehabilitation for Polavaram Dam evacuees
records.name: Renuka Chowdhury
records.min_name: WATER RESOURCES, RIVER DEVELOPMENT AND GANGA REJUVENATION
records.qn_text: (a) whether it is a fact that the tribal evacuees subjected to submergence under the Polavaram Major Irrigation Project have not received their share under the Relief and Rehabilitation Package even after a decade; <br/><br/>(b) if so, the details thereof, along with the reasons therefor; and <br/><br/>(c) the corrective steps taken by Government to investigate the charges of large scale misappropriation in first phase of compensation?<br/>
records.ans_text: THE MINISTER OF STATE FOR WATER RESOURCES, RIVER DEVELOPMENT AND GANGA REJUVENATION & PARLIAMENTARY AFFAIRS<br/><br/>(SHRI ARJUN RAM MEGHWAL)<br/><br/>(a)	to  (c) Polavaram Project is being executed by Govt. of Andhra Pradesh on behalf of Govt. of India. As reported by the State Government of Andhra Pradesh, total number of Project Displaced Families (PDFs)/Project Affected Families (PAFs) from the submergence of Polavaram project is 98818, out of which 55113 are Scheduled Tribes (STs). As on 28.02.2018, an area of 3833.68 acre has been acquired incurring an expenditure of Rs.130.97 Cr and provided to 1774 ST PDFs covering 30 habitations under provision of land for land.  Further, the R&R entitlements of Rs.27.52 Cr have been paid to 1351 ST PDFs, and out of them 1019 have been shifted to Rehabilitation and Resettlement (R&R) centres.<br/><br/>The works of R&R are being carried out by the State Government.  They have intimated that there is no misappropriation in respect of disbursement of the Rehabilitation and Resettlement package to the PDFs.<br/><br/>*****<br/>

records.qtitle: Utilisation of CAMPA fund
records.name: Renuka Chowdhury
records.qn_text: (a)	whether the rules governing the CAMPA fund have not yet been finalized;<br/>(b)	if so, the details thereof along with the reasons for delay; and<br/>(c)	the steps taken by Government for proper user of CAMPA funds for implementation of agro-forestry in non-forest land, to compensate for felled forest across the country?<br/>
records.ans_text: MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF ENVIRONMENT, FOREST AND CLIMATE CHANGE <br/><br/>(DR. MAHESH SHARMA)<br/><br/>(a)&(b) Sir, the Gazette Notification of Draft Compensatory Afforestation Fund Rule, 2018 has been published on 17th February, 2018 for obtaining comments / suggestions from the stakeholders. <br/><br/>(c) 	The compensatory afforestation is done on non-forest land and degraded forest land to compensate the forest loss due to diversion of forest land for developmental work. The Compensatory Afforestation Fund will be utilized as per the provisions of Compensatory Afforestation Fund Act, 2016 and the Compensatory Afforestation Rules made thereof  which provides for massive Afforestation Programme in the State affected due to diversion of forests for development works.   <br/>***<br/>

records.qtitle: Upkeep of railway infrastructure
records.name: Renuka Chowdhury
records.qn_text: (a)	whether it is a fact that the number of accidents has increased in the recent past due to accumulated deficit in upkeep of railway infrastructure as a result of decades of neglect;<br/><br/>(b)	if so, the reasons therefor along with the number of such accidents occurred during the last three years, Zone-wise; and<br/><br/>(c)	the steps taken by Government to formulate an action plan for regular upkeep of railway infrastructure?<br/><br/><br/>
records.ans_text: MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF RAILWAYS<br/><br/>(SHRI RAJEN GOHAIN)<br/><br/><br/>(a) to (c): No, Sir. Safety is given the topmost priority.  Assets are maintained as per standards codified in the various manuals. As a result, number of consequential train accidents (including accidents at Unmanned Level Crossings mainly caused due to negligence of road vehicle users)  have decreased from 135 in 2014-15, to 107 in 2015-16 and further to 104 in 2016-17.  In the current year (upto 28th  February, 2018) the number of consequential train accidents have further reduced to 70 as compared to 99 in the corresponding period of the previous year<br/><br/><br/>*****<br/>

records.qtitle: Compensation to persons convicted wrongly
records.name: Renuka Chowdhury
records.qn_text: <br/>(a) whether there is any mechanism to seek recourse to justice or demand compensation for those wrongly incarcerated;<br/>(b) if so, the details thereof and if not, the reasons therefor; and<br/>(c) the steps taken by Government to codify specific law for providing compensation to persons accused of or convicted wrongly?<br/>
records.ans_text: ANSWER<br/>MINISTER OF STATE FOR LAW &JUSTICE AND CORPORATE AFFAIRS<br/>(SH. P.P.Chaudhary)<br/>(a) to (c) Law Commission of India in its 243rd Report has recommended for raising of compensation limit under Section 358 of Cr.PC (Compensation to persons groundlessly arrested). The proposal is under examination in the Ministry of Home Affairs.<br/>

records.qtitle: Utilisation certificates for pre  post matric scholarships
records.name: Renuka Chowdhury
records.qn_text: (a) the total amount released to States for pre and post matric scholarships to SC/ ST students during the last three years, State-wise and year-wise; <br/>(b) whether a number of States have not furnished utilisation certificates in respect of the scholarships and if so, the details thereof; and <br/>(c) the steps taken by Government for timely release of scholarships to SC/ST students?<br/>
records.ans_text: MINISTER OF STATE FOR SOCIAL JUSTICE AND EMPOWERMENT<br/>(SHRI VIJAY SAMPLA)<br/><br/>(a): Central Assistance is released to States/UTs under Centrally Sponsored Schemes of Post matric and Pre-Matric Scholarship to SC/ST students. The details of total amount released to States/UTs for Pre and Post Matric Scholarships to SC/ ST students during the last three years State-wise is attached at Annexure-I to IV.<br/><br/>(b) The state-wise details of due utilization Certificates not furnished by States under Pre-matric and Post matric Scholarship Schemes to SC/ST students is attached at Annexure V and VI.<br/><br/>(c) States/UTs have been advised to ensure payment of scholarships directly to the accounts of the beneficiaries. Besides this, regular follow up through correspondence, meeting with State Government officials and regional conferences are done to ensure submission of requisite documents for expeditious release of Central Assistance under the scholarship Schemes.<br/>******<br/>

records.qtitle: Database of housing projects
records.name: Renuka Chowdhury
records.qn_text: Will the Minister of HOUSING AND URBAN AFFAIRS be pleased to state:<br/><br/>(a) 	whether Government proposes to have a central database of all the housing projects to capture their status and delays; <br/><br/>(b) 	if so, the details thereof and if not, the reasons therefor; and<br/><br/>(c)	the steps taken by Government for strict implementation of Real Estate Regulation Act to ensure time-bound delivery of housing projects by the builders?<br/><br/><br/>
records.ans_text: THE MINISTER OF STATE (INDEPENDENT CHARGE) OF THE MINISTRY OF HOUSING AND URBAN AFFAIRS<br/><br/>(SHRI HARDEEP SINGH PURI)<br/><br/><br/>(a) to (c):	The States/Union Territories (UTs) and the Real Estate Regulatory Authority constituted under the Real Estate (Regulation and Development) Act, 2016 (Act) are to ensure the registration of ongoing projects as per Section 3(1) of the Act and to publish and maintain a website of records, for public viewing, of all real estate projects for which registration has been given, with such details as may be prescribed, including information provided in the application for which registration has been granted.<br/><br/>	The Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs has during workshops, State level review meetings and interactions emphasized the need to ensure implementation of the Act through framing of Rules by States / UTs and establishment of Real Estate Regulatory Authority and Real Estate Appellate Tribunal. <br/>	<br/>                     *****<br/><br/>

records.qtitle: Blending of methanol in petrol
records.name: Renuka Chowdhury
records.qn_text: (a)   whether Government is considering blending of methanol in petrol;<br/>(b)   if so, the details thereof; and <br/>(c)   how far this step is likely to reduce pollution and make petrol cheaper?<br/><br/>
records.ans_text: MINISTER OF PETROLEUM & NATURAL GAS <br/> (SHRI DHARMENDRA PRADHAN)<br/><br/>(a) & (b) : To take forward the initiative of methanol economy in India, the Government has taken the following steps :<br/><br/>(i)   NITI Aayog has constituted “Apex Committee on Methanol Economy” and five task forces to study various aspects of Methanol production and usage of its blend in gasoline in transport sector.<br/>  <br/>(ii)   BIS has set up a committee to finalise the methanol gasoline blend (M15) specifications.  <br/><br/>(iii)  Automotive Research Association of India (ARAI) has started studies to establish the performance of Methanol Blend (15 per cent) in Gasoline and its efficacy to reduce pollution.<br/><br/>  <br/>(c):  Though methanol has more efficient and cleaner burning, it has nearly half the volumetric energy content of gasoline, indicating that it would require double quantity and price for the same energy output. <br/><br/>******<br/><br/>

records.qtitle: Private participation in ABWs
records.name: Renuka Chowdhury
records.qn_text: (a) whether it is a fact that the Ministry has decided to allow private firms to operate all the Army Base Workshops (ABWs);<br/><br/><br/>(b) if so, the details thereof and the reasons therefor; and <br/><br/>(c) the steps taken by Government to enhance combat capability and rebalance the defence expenditure of the armed forces?<br/>
records.ans_text: MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF DEFENCE<br/>DR. SUBHASH BHAMRE<br/><br/><br/>(a) to (c):  The Government had constituted a Committee of Experts (CoE) to study and recommend measures to enhance combat capabilities and re-balance defence expenditure.  Based on the recommendations of the Committee in respect of Army Base Workshops (ABWs), the Government has approved operation of 8 Army Base Workshops (ABWs) on Government Owned Contractor Operated (GOCO) model.<br/><br/>          Some of the other major recommendations made by the Committee for enhancement of combat capabilities and rebalancing of defence expenditure, which have been approved for implementation, inter-alia include optimization of Signals Establishments, restructuring of repair echelons in the Army, restructuring and redeployment of Ordnance echelons, Supply and Transportation echelons, Animal Transport Units, Closure of Military Farms and Army Postal Establishments in peace locations, etc.<br/><br/>******<br/>

records.name: Renuka Chowdhury

records.qn_text: (a) whether Government has decided to create 100 lakh MT storage capacity in the form of steel silos;<br/>(b) if so, the details thereof along with the locations identified for the purpose across the country; and<br/>(c) by when the construction of steel silos is likely to be completed and made available for storage of foodgrains?
records.ans_text: MINISTER OF STATE FOR CONSUMER AFFAIRS, FOOD & PUBLIC DISTRIBUTION<br/>(SHRI C. R. CHAUDHARY)<br/>(a) & (b): Yes, Sir. Government of India has approved a road map for construction of steel silos in the country for a capacity of 100 Lakh MT (LMT) in 3 phases by 2020. Private parties selected through tendering process will construct the silos to be taken on guaranteed hiring by Food Corporation of India (FCI)/State Agencies. Total 31.50 LMT is planned to be constructed by Government of India through FCI & Central Warehousing Corporation (CWC). Balance capacity of 68.50 LMT is to be constructed by the State Governments/Agencies.<br/>The location-wise and State-wise details of silos planned for construction are at Annexure.<br/>(c): The technology for rice silos is yet to be established and FCI has undertaken pilot projects at 2 places namely Kaimur and Buxar in Bihar. For the rest of the capacity, the construction of silos is dependent on the selection/approval of sites and sidings, which are dependent on the respective State Governments and Railways. Further, construction of silos to be done by State Governments depends on their response which has been lacking. records.qtitle: MSP for fruits and vegetables
records.name: Renuka Chowdhury
records.qn_text: (a) 	whether Government is considering to fix Minimum Support Prices (MSPs) for fruits and vegetables;<br/><br/>(b) 	if so, the details thereof and if not, the reasons therefor; and<br/><br/>(c) 	the steps taken by Government to provide remunerative prices to fruit and vegetable growing farmers in order to improve their condition?<br/>
records.ans_text: MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF AGRICULTURE AND FARMERS WELFARE<br/><br/>( SHRI GAJENDRA SINGH SHEKHAWAT)  <br/><br/>(a) to (c):	Government fixes Minimum Support Prices (MSPs) for 22 major agricultural crops viz. Paddy, Jowar, Bajra, Maize, Ragi, Arhar, Moong, Urad, Groundnut-in-shell, Soyabean, Sunflower, Sesamum, Nigerseed, Cotton, Wheat, Barley, Gram, Masur (Lentil), Rapeseed/Mustard, Safflower, Jute and Copra and Fair & Remunerative Price (FRP) for Sugarcane on the basis of the recommendations of the Commission for Agricultural Costs & Prices (CACP), after obtaining the views of State Governments and Central Ministries/Departments concerned and other relevant factors. In addition, MSP for Toria and De-Husked coconut is also fixed on the basis of MSPs of Rapeseed/Mustard and Copra respectively. <br/><br/>Government implements Market Intervention Scheme (MIS) for procurement of agricultural and horticultural crops including fruits and vegetables which are not covered under the MSP on the request of State/UT Governments. The MIS is implemented in order to protect the growers of these commodities from making distress sale in the event of bumper crop when the prices tend to fall below the economic level/cost of production. Losses, if any, incurred by the procuring agencies are shared by the Central Government and the concerned State Government on 50:50 basis (75:25 in case of North-Eastern States).<br/><br/>In addition, Government under Mission for Integrated Development of Horticulture (MIDH) scheme is supporting farmers producer organization and post production activities including pack houses, cold storages, marketing infrastructure to ensure remunerative prices for farmers.<br/><br/><br/>*****<br/>

records.qtitle: Fake enrolment in Anganwadis
records.name: Renuka Chowdhury
records.qn_text: (a)	whether Government is aware of fake enrolment of children in Aganwadis across the country; <br/><br/>(b)	if so, the outcome of the pilot study conducted in this regard in certain States particularly in Assam; and <br/><br/>(c)	the steps taken by Government to check large scale pilferage of funds meant for Anganwadis?<br/>
records.ans_text: MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF WOMEN AND CHILD DEVELOPMENT<br/>(DR. VIRENDRA KUMAR)<br/><br/>(a)	No, Sir. No such incidence has come to the notice of the Government. <br/><br/>(b)	Does not arise.<br/><br/>(c)	As regards checking the pilferage of funds, the Government of India has prescribed a 5 tier monitoring Committees at the National, State, District, Block and Anganwadi Centre (AWC) levels. The data of the services rendered at the AWCs are generated by the Anganwadi Workers and is transmitted upwards which is reported to this Ministry every month by the State Governments as consolidated by them. For quick on-line transmission of data, Rapid Reporting System is in operation. <br/><br/>*******<br/>

records.qtitle: Withdrawal of recognition by NCTE
records.name: Renuka Chowdhury
records.qn_text: (a) whether the National council for Teachers Education (NCTE) has withdrawn recognition<br/>from thousands of teachers'' education institutes in the recent past;<br/>(b) if so, the details thereof along with the reasons therefor, State-wise; and<br/>(c) the steps taken by Government to make available names of the recognized teacher<br/>education institutes on the website of NCTE for informalion of students seeking admission in<br/>recognized institutes and also to shutdown unrecognized institutions?
records.ans_text: <br/>MINISTER OF THE STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HUMAN RESOURCE DEVELOPMENT<br/>(SHRI UPENDRA KUSHWAHA)<br/><br/>(a & b): During the academic session 2016-2017, the NCTE had withdrawn recognition of 133<br/>institutions offering various Teacher Educataon Programmes (TEPs) for not following the<br/>guidelines stipulated in the NCTE, Act, Rules and Norms and Standards. A state-wise list of<br/>institutions is attached at Annexure-l<br/><br/>(c):The list of recognized institutions as well the withdrawn institutions is available on the<br/>website of the concerned Regional Committee (s) and NCTE Headquarters which is being<br/>regularly updated. The above list can be seen at http://ncte-india.org/ncte_<br/>new/pdf/Affidavit_showcause_Recognitioncourse after 13th Dec2016 13.07.2017.pdf.

records.qtitle: Regulatory mechanism for deemed universities
records.name: Renuka Chowdhury
records.qn_text: (a) whether Government has any regulatory and oversight mechanism for deemed universities; <br/>(b) if so, the details thereof and if not, the reasons therefor; and <br/>(c) the remedial steps taken by Government in this regard for the benefit of students?<br/>
records.ans_text: <br/>MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HUMAN RESOURCE DEVELOPMENT<br/>(DR. SATYA PAL SINGH)<br/><br/>(a) to (c): Yes, Sir. In exercise of powers conferred under clauses [f] & [g] of sub-section [1] of Section 26 of the University Grants Commission (UGC) Act, 1956, UGC has notified the UGC (Institutions Deemed to be Universities) Regulations, 2016 to regulate the institution deemed to be universities. These Regulations are available on UGC website www.ugc.ac.in. <br/>	In addition, this Ministry has constituted a Committee to suggest a oversight mechanism to regulate the Deemed to be Universities as per the Order dated 03.11.2017 of Hon’ble Supreme Court in Civil Appeal No. in Civil Appeal Nos. 17869-17870/2017.<br/>*****<br/>

records.qtitle: Setting up of societies by ESIC for time bound delivery of services
records.name: Renuka Chowdhury
records.qn_text: (a)whether the Employees'' State Insurance Corporation (ESIC) proposes to set up societies across the country for time-bound delivery of services to its beneficiaries;<br/>(b)if so, the details thereof along with financial cost involved; and<br/>(c)the steps taken by Government to transfer the reimbursement amount to beneficiaries with due diligence in a timebound manner?<br/>
records.ans_text: MINISTER OF STATE (IC) FOR LABOUR AND EMPLOYMENT<br/>(SHRI SANTOSH KUMAR GANGWAR)<br/><br/>(a) & (b):	The 46th Indian Labour Conference held on 20th and 21st July, 2015 in one of its recommendations stated that “The ESIC should directly run the health services in all the States, state should not be asked to bear the cost of medical expenses.” Therefore, the matter was taken up in 166th meeting of the ESI Corporation on 07.08.2015, a sub-committee was formed. In the 167th meeting, the sub-committee submitted its report and it was decided to form State Autonomous Body under Section 58(5) of the ESI Act, 1948. Structure of the State Autonomous Body was circulated and all state Governments were informed to constitute a State Autonomous Body by 31.03.2017 so as to be eligible for 100% expenditure up to the ceiling from ESIC. Due to some states going for assembly election, deadline was further extended to 30.06.2017.<br/>Contd..2/-<br/>::  2  ::<br/>14 states accepted the proposal for State Autonomous Body and are entitled to get the benefit of 100% bearing of expenditure up to the ceiling, laid down from time to time, by ESI Corporation subject to them forming State Autonomous Body/Society as per structure approved by Corporation in its 172nd meeting held on 06.12.2017. However, for rest of the states existing arrangement of sharing expenditure in the ratio of 7/8:1/8 shall continue. For the states forming State Autonomous Body/Society, funds shall be directly transferred to the Society which is likely to enhance the medical benefit service delivery in respective states under ESI Scheme available to its beneficiaries.<br/>(c):	From time to time, ESI Corporation has undertaken steps to ensure due diligence while processing reimbursement claim of ESI beneficiaries. The steps taken include administrative reform measures and Information Technology (IT)/ online processing of such reimbursement claims. In addition, CPGRAMS also monitors such cases at ESIC Head Quarter.<br/><br/>******<br/>

records.qtitle: Status of fencing work along Indo  Bangladesh border
records.name: Renuka Chowdhury
records.qn_text: (a) the present status of fencing work along the Indo-Bangladesh border;<br/><br/>(b) the reasons for very slow progress in the fencing work; and<br/><br/>(c) the steps taken by Government to tackle illegal influx of immigrants including Rohingyas through Indo- Bangladesh border?
records.ans_text: MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HOME AFFAIRS<br/>(SHRI KIREN RIJIJU)<br/><br/>(a) & (b):	Out of the 3326 km of sanctioned length of fence along Indo-Bangladesh Border, 2746.44 km has been completed. The land acquisition process on Indo-Bangladesh Border is time consuming and cumbersome due to which the progress has been slow. In addition to pending land acquisition, limited working seasons due to heavy rainfall, extended rainy season in the North-Eastern parts of the country and difficult terrain conditions have been affecting the pace of the work. <br/>(c):	The Government has adopted a multipronged approach for security arrangements at the borders to tackle illegal influx of immigrants including Rohingyas. The arrangements include deployment of Border Guarding Force (BGF), construction of border fence, construction of border roads, installation of floodlights, construction of Border Out Posts (BOPs), introduction of Hi-tech surveillance equipments, besides identifying vulnerable BOPs, etc.  										<br/><br/><br/><br/> <br/>                       *********

records.qtitle: Installation of donation boxes at Mahatma Gandhis Memorial at Rajghat
records.name: Renuka Chowdhury
records.qn_text: (a) whether Government has allowed installation of donation boxes at Mahatma Gandhi’s Memorial at Rajghat;<br/><br/>(b) if so, the reasons therefor; and<br/><br/>(c) the steps taken by Government for proper maintenance of Rajghat as well as removal of donation boxes, disrespectful to the Father of the Nation?<br/>
records.ans_text: MINISTER OF STATE (I/C) FOR CULTURE AND MINISTER OF STATE FOR ENVIRONMENT, FOREST AND CLIMATE CHANGE<br/><br/>(DR. MAHESH SHARMA)<br/><br/>(a) to (c): 	Under the Rajghat Samadhi Act, 1951, Rajghat Samadhi Committee (RSC) had been constituted with a mandate to keep the Samadhi in proper order. The RSC, in its 27th meeting held on 06.09.1961 passed a resolution for placing the donation boxes in the Rajghat Complex. This resolution was based on the Government of India’s letter No. 3250-WS/53 dated 12.06.1953. The donations are collected by the Harijan Sevak Sangh to be utilized for the welfare of the people belonging to dalit communities. RSC is functioning as per its mandate and taking all necessary steps for maintenance of Rajghat Complex. No decision has been taken for removal of donation boxes from Samadhi Complex. <br/><br/>************<br/>

records.qtitle: Detection of new leprosy cases
records.name: Renuka Chowdhury
records.qn_text: Will the Minister of HEALTH AND FAMILY WELFARE be pleased to state:<br/><br/>(a) whether a large number of new leprosy cases have been detected across the country in the recent past;<br/><br/>(b) if so, the details thereof for the last three years along with the reasons therefor, State-wise; and<br/><br/>(c) the fresh steps taken by Government to eliminate leprosy as a public health problem by 2020 as envisaged under National Leprosy Elimination Programme?<br/>
records.ans_text: ANSWER<br/>THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HEALTH AND <br/>FAMILY WELFARE<br/>(SHRI ASHWINI KUMAR CHOUBEY)<br/>(a) & (b):  Yes. During 2016-17, number of new leprosy cases reported by various States/UTs were 1,35,485 as compared to 1,27,334 cases reported during 2015-16.  This increase of 6.4% in new cases was the result of the new strategy of active case detection.  A statement indicating States/UTs wise details of new cases of leprosy detected during last three years is at Annexure.<br/><br/>(c):	Under National Leprosy Eradication Programme (NLEP) the following fresh steps have been taken:-<br/>(i)	Introduction of three pronged strategy to detect leprosy cases  which includes:<br/>a)	Leprosy Case Detection Campaign (LCDC)<br/>b)	Focused Leprosy Campaign;<br/>c)	Case detection in hard to reach areas; <br/>(ii)	Sparsh Leprosy Awareness Campaign introduced to tackle stigma and discrimination against leprosy patients.<br/><br/>As a result of the above steps, percentage of Grade II Disability amongst the new cases has come down significantly.<br/> <br/>

records.qtitle: Regulatory mechanism for crypto currency
records.name: Renuka Chowdhury
records.qn_text: (a)   :        whether Government had constituted an inter-disciplinary panel to look into legality of crypto currencies and suggest a way forward; <br/>(b)   :	if so, the details thereof along with its outcome; and <br/>(c)   :	the steps taken by Government to have a regulatory mechanism for online purchase and sale of crypto currencies in the country ? <br/>
records.ans_text: MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF FINANCE<br/>(SHRI Pon. RADHAKRISHNAN)<br/><br/>(a) to (c) : The Department of Economic Affairs had constituted an Inter-Disciplinary Committee to take stock of the present status of Virtual Currencies. The committee invited feedback from public and submitted its report. Subsequently, a Committee under the Chairmanship of Secretary, Department of Economic Affairs has been constituted for deliberating over all issues related to virtual currencies to propose specific actions to be taken. The Government has issued a statement on December 29, 2017 cautioning the people against the risks of investing in virtual currencies.  The Reserve Bank of India has also cautioned the users, holders and traders of Virtual Currencies from time to time, about the potential financial, operational, legal, customer protection and security related risks.  <br/>********<br/>

records.qtitle: Delay in release of daily labour wages in MGNREGA
records.name: Renuka Chowdhury
records.qn_text: (a) 	the total daily wage labour dues pending under MGNREGA to be released to Telangana and Andhra Pradesh as on date; <br/><br/>(b) 	the reasons for delay in release of labour wage dues; and <br/><br/>(c) 	the steps taken by Government for early release of pending daily wage labour dues under MGNREGA?<br/>
records.ans_text: MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF RURAL DEVELOPMENT<br/>(SHRI RAM KRIPAL YADAV)<br/><br/>(a) & (b):	The Ministry along with the States/UTs has been making concerted efforts for improving the timely payment of wages. States/ UTs have been advised to generate pay orders in time. This has resulted in considerable improvement in the status of timely generation of pay order and leading to improvement in actual time taken to credit wages in the workers account. During the current financial year 85.75% and 87.91% payments have been generated within 15 days in respect of Telangana and Andhra Pradesh (as on 01.02.2018) respectively.  The delay in payment of wages is due to implementation issues in the States which include inadequate staffing, non-timely recording and reporting of attendance, measurement, data entry, generation of wage list, Fund Transfer Order (FTO), Public Financial Management System and Banks/ Post offices related issues etc.<br/><br/>(c):	Efforts have been made by the Ministry to reduce the delay in payment of wages to the MGNREGA workers viz., timely release of funds, payment through National Electronic Fund Management System (NeFMS) for direct payment of wages into workers accounts, issuance of guidelines for monitoring of timely payment and payment of delay compensation, enabling appropriate provisions in NREGASoft to monitor timely payment of wages and payment of delay compensation. The Ministry is in constant engagement with the State Governments/ UTs through review meetings, video conferences, Mid Term Review, SMS based monitoring etc.<br/> <br/>	<br/>*****<br/><br/><br/><br/><br/><br/><br/>
