records.qtitle: Districts with high incidence of Leprosy
records.name: Renuka Chowdhury
records.qn_text: Will the Minister of HEALTH AND FAMILY WELFARE be pleased to state:<br/><br/>(a) the total number of districts having high incidence of Leprosy in the country, State-wise;<br/><br/>(b) whether in certain States children too are reporting Leprosy related deformities and if so, the details thereof along with the reasons therefor; and<br/><br/>(c) the corrective steps taken by Government for elimination of Leprosy from the country?<br/>
records.ans_text: ANSWER<br/>THE MINISTER OF HEALTH AND FAMILY WELFARE<br/>(SHRI JAGAT PRAKASH NADDA)<br/>(a):	The total number of districts reported Prevalence Rate (PR)>1/10,000 population as on 31st March, 2016 were 107. The State/UT wise number of districts having PR>1/10,000 population is at Annexure I.<br/><br/>(b):	Yes, children too are reporting leprosy related deformities. Status of state wise child cases is placed at Annexure II.<br/>(c):	The corrective  steps taken by Government for elimination of leprosy are as below :-<br/>(i)	Leprosy Case Detection Campaign (LCDC) is being carried out in high endemic districts with a focus on early detection and treatment of cases so as to arrest further transmission and to prevent occurrence of deformities.	In the above activity, physical examination of whole population is done with the aim to detect all cases of leprosy in high endemic districts. This activity was carried out in 50 high endemic districts of 7 States (in March-April, 2016). In the current year also, similar Leprosy Case Detection Campaign is planned in 163 districts of 20 States/UTs.  <br/><br/><br/><br/>(ii)	Decentralized integrated leprosy services through General Health Care system and House hold contact surveys of Multibacillary (MB) & child cases are being carried out.<br/>(iii)	Accredited Social Health Activists (ASHA) are being involved in the detection and complete treatment of Leprosy cases.<br/>(iv)	Disability Prevention & Medical Rehabilitation (DPMR) services are being strengthened.  <br/><br/>(v)	Information, Education & Communication (IEC) activities are being carried out in the community to improve self reporting to Primary Health Centre (PHC) and for reduction of stigma.<br/>(vi)	Intensive monitoring and supervision of the programme is being done by District, State and Central Government authorities.  <br/> <br/>

records.qtitle: Stressed Asset Fund for curbing NPAs
records.name: Renuka Chowdhury
records.qn_text: a)	whether the Government proposes to set up a Stressed Asset Fund to fight NPAs of Public Sector Banks ;<br/><br/>b)	if so ,the details thereof; and<br/><br/>c)	the steps taken by Government to evolve an efficient resolution and recovery process for the Public Sector Banks affected by burgeoning NPAs?<br/><br/><br/>
records.ans_text: THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF FINANCE<br/><br/>(a)	& (b): No. However, Indian Banks’ Association (IBA) had taken up with Reserve bank Of India (RBI) regarding creation of Special Situation Fund (SSF) to provide a viable solution for the stressed accounts with an objective to:<br/>i.	Take-over viable assets from the lenders and guide the management of the company to make the company economically viable.<br/>ii.	Provide priority debt/equity for working capital or for project completion for companies that may not fully be held by them. <br/>In response RBI has informed IBA that banks may set up two different funds viz. Stressed Assets Equity Fund (SAEF) and Stressed Asset Lending Fund (SALF) instead of one Special Situation Fund.<br/>(c): The government has taken specific measures to address issues in sectors such as Infrastructure (Power, Roads etc.), Steel and Textiles, where incidence of NPAs is high. The government has also approved establishment of six (6) new Debt Recovery Tribunals (DRTs), to speed up the recovery of bad loans of the banking sector, in addition to existing thirty three. Reserve Bank of India (RBI) has also undertaken steps which include (i) Formation of Joint Lenders’ Forum (JLF) for revitalizing stressed assets in the system, (ii) Flexible Structuring for long term project loans to Infrastructure and Core industries, and (iii) Strategic Debt Restructuring (SDR) scheme. (iv) Scheme for Sustainable Structuring of Stressed Assets (S4A).The Government has recently issued advisory to banks to take action against guarantors in event of default by borrower under relevant sections of SARFAESI Act, Indian Contract Act & RDDB&FI Act, since in the event of default; the liability of the guarantor is co-extensive with the borrower.<br/>*************<br/>

records.qtitle: Steps to prevent fire at ammunition depots
records.name: Renuka Chowdhury
records.qn_text: (a) whether it is a fact that ammunition depots are functioning with risk of fire accident as the equipment and manpower are not held as per the requirement and authorisations;<br/><br/>(b) if so, the reasons for a number of deficiencies in the fire fighting and safety mechanism of ammunition depots including storage of large quantity of ammunition in temporary accommodation;<br/><br/>(c) the details of fire incidents in ammunition depots during the last three years along with losses incurred; and<br/><br/>(d) the corrective steps taken by Government to prevent fire in ammunition depots in future?<br/>
records.ans_text: MINISTER OF DEFENCE<br/>           SHRI MANOHAR PARRIKAR<br/><br/><br/>(a) & (b):  Due to delay in procurement / recruitment, the deficiencies of 23 fire fighting trucks and 362 personnel exist in ammunition depots of Indian Army.<br/><br/>Ammunition is stored in permanent accommodation.  However, due to operational and other local exigencies, some ammunition is stored in temporary sheds.<br/><br/>(c)  The only major fire incident in ammunition depot during last three years has occurred in Central Ammunition Depot, Pulgaon on 31st May, 2016.  There were 19 fatal and 17 non-fatal casualties, and the total loss of equipment and stores as per preliminary estimation is approximately Rs.7.90 crores.<br/><br/>(d)  On the basis of the recommendations of Court of Inquiry and subsequent deliberations with all stakeholders, the following has been approved by the Government in order to prevent recurrence of such incidents:-<br/><br/>(i)	Disposal of all defective segregated mines (Anti Tank Mines 1A ND) for exudation of TNT, held at various locations will be undertaken by Army Headquarters (AHQ).<br/>(ii)	Ordnance Factory Board (OFB) will replace or repair the defective ammunition within three months. <br/>(iii)	Army Headquarters in consultation with all stakeholders will finalize the Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs’) for:<br/>(a)Disposal of defective ammunition in fixed time frame, and<br/>(b)Fixing up responsibility for defect and regularization of loss.<br/><br/>(iv) 	Department of Defence Production (DDP) in consultation with all stakeholders will prepare a SOP for handholding of Production Agency by the Designer till production stabilizes.<br/>(v)	Army Headquarters will review the security (including surveillance) and fire safety arrangements at all ammunition depots.<br/><br/>*******<br/>

records.qtitle: Development of inland waterways in Goa
records.name: Renuka Chowdhury
records.qn_text: (a) 	whether Government plans to develop inland waterways in Goa by dredging six of its rivers; <br/>(b) if so, the details thereof; and<br/>(c) the steps taken by Government to protect the marine ecology of the rivers from impact of dredging? <br/>
records.ans_text: ANSWER<br/>            MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF SHIPPING<br/>(SHRI  PON RADHAKRISHNAN)<br/><br/>(a)&(b):The following six waterways in Goa have been declared as National Waterways (NWs) underthe National Waterways Act, 2016:-<br/>i)	Mandovi River (NW-68) – from Bridge at Usgoan to confluence of Mandovi River with Arabian Sea at Reis Magos (41 km). <br/><br/>ii)	Zuari River (NW-111) – from Sanvordem  Bridge to Marmugao Port (50 km).<br/>iii)	Chapora River (NW-25) – from Bridge at State Highway No. 124 (1 km from Maneri village) to confluence of Chaporariver with Arabian Sea at Morjim (33 km).<br/>iv)	Cumberjua Canal (NW-27) – from Confluence of Cumberjua and Zuari rivers near Cortalim ferry terminal to confluence of Cumberjua and Mandovi rivers near Sao MartiasVidhanParishad (17 km).<br/>v)	Mapusa River (NW-71) – from Bridge on National Highway – 17 at Mapusa to confluence point of Mapusa and Mandovi Rivers at Porvorim (27 km).<br/>vi)	Sal River (NW-88) – from OrlimDeusa Bridge to confluence with Arabian Sea at Mobor (14 km).<br/><br/>Development of these NWs is undertaken through various measures including dredging based on the recommendations in feasibility/ Detailed Project Reports (DPRs).  These reports for NWs on Mandovi and Zuari rivers have been completed. <br/><br/>(c):	To minimize the adverse impact of developmental works on the marine ecology, if any, the recommendations of  detailed Environment Impact Assessment (EIA)/ Environment Management Plan (EMP)/ Coastal Regulation Zone (CRZ) and Wild Life Clearance studies commissioned for NW-68 and NW-111 would be taken into account.<br/>*****<br/><br/>

records.qtitle: Timely payment of wages under MGNREGA
records.name: Renuka Chowdhury
records.qn_text: (a) 	whether there is no provision under MGNREGA to compensate workers whose wages have been delayed by more than the stipulated period of 15 days; <br/><br/>(b) 	if so, the reasons for tardy implementation of Supreme Court orders in this regard; and<br/> <br/>(c) 	the fresh steps taken by Government to ensure timely payment of wages of workers under the scheme across the country?<br/><br/>
records.ans_text: MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF RURAL DEVELOPMENT<br/>(SHRI RAM KRIPAL YADAV)<br/><br/>(a)&(b):	To reduce the delay in payment of wages under Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Act (MGNREGA), a system of payment of compensation for such delays was brought in Para 29 of Schedule II of the Act. The States/UTs have been advised to ensure compliance with this provision. The following steps are taken to check the delays in wage payment:<br/><br/>(i)     State Government has been advised to notify the ‘Rules’ and implement the 	system of compensation for delay in wage payment.<br/><br/>(ii)    State Government has been advised to review and discuss with the Programme Officers periodically the issues of delayed payments.<br/><br/>(c):	In order to ensure timely payment wages, Rules have been issued for timely payment of wages under which, it was suggested that clear accountability shall be fixed on the functionaries for timely performance of specific duties leading to payment of wages. <br/><br/>For ensuring timely payment of wages, the Central Government has also started National Electronic Fund Management System (NeFMS) in 11 States (Assam, Bihar, Haryana, Karnataka, Kerala, Odisha, Punjab, Rajasthan, Tripura, Uttar Pradesh and Uttrakhand) and launched Dashboard for tracking of pending Fund Transfer Orders, Public Fund Management System, electronic Fund Management System, Direct Benefit Transfer.<br/><br/>*****<br/>

records.qtitle: Passing on incentives of Mega Food Park Scheme to farmers
records.name: Renuka Chowdhury
records.qn_text: (a)	whether Government has evolved any mechanism to ensure that the produce of farmers are taken by the Food Processing Industries (FPIs) at remunerative and prescribed prices, if so, the details thereof; and<br/><br/>(b)	the steps taken by Government to ensure that the incentives of the Mega Food Park Scheme are passed on to the farmers or some percentage of profits is earmarked for the farmers whose produce are taken by the FPIs?<br/>
records.ans_text: THE MINISTER OF STATE FOR FOOD PROCESSING INDUSTRIES <br/>(SADHVI NIRANJAN JYOTI)<br/><br/>(a)	The large gap between the need and availability of infrastructural facilities along the supply chain in the food processing sector has resulted in huge wastage and loss at each stage of the supply chain and ultimately loss to the farmers. Mega Food Park Scheme aims to provide a mechanism to bring together farmers, processors and retailers and link agriculture production to the market so as to ensure maximization of value addition, minimization of wastages and increase in farmers’ income.<br/>Mega Food Park (MFP) provides modern infrastructure facilities for the food processing along the value chain from the farm to the market with a cluster based approach based on a hub and spokes model. It includes creation of infrastructure for primary processing and storage near the farm in the form of Primary Processing Centres (PPCs) and Collection Centres (CCs) and common facilities and enabling infrastructure at Central Processing Centre (CPC). These PPCs and CCs act as aggregation and storage points to feed raw material to the processing units located in the CPC. Each Mega Food Park is likely to benefit about 25000-30000 farmers. However, there is no mechanism to purchase produce of farmers at prescribed prices. <br/><br/>(b)	Farmers are one of the direct beneficiaries of the MFPs if, they are part of the Special Purpose Vehicle (SPV), which implements, own and operate the projects. Indirectly, sourcing of raw material by the processing units inside MFP and value addition of farmer’s produce results in increase of the farmer’s income. They may also avail sorting, grading and storage facilities created by MFPs for value addition and enhancement of shelf life of their produce. These projects are also helping in increasing the income of farmers by increasing export of frozen and packed farm products, use of waste bi-products of the fruits and vegetable by adding value to them and direct/indirect employment generation etc. Development of such processing clusters will also help in latest technology adoption in the production systems and better returns to the farmers. <br/><br/>********<br/>

records.qtitle: Setting up of National Grasslands Authority
records.name: Renuka Chowdhury
records.qn_text: (a) whether Government proposes to set up a National Grasslands Authority;<br/> (b) if so, the details thereof, along with its aims and objectives; and<br/> (c) the steps taken by Government to tackle the problem of fodder shortage due to shrinking grazing grounds and grassland cover in the country, especially in drought affected States?<br/>
records.ans_text: ANSWER<br/><br/>THE MINISTER OF STATE FOR AGRICULTURE AND FARMERS WELFARE<br/>(DR. SANJEEV KUMAR BALYAN)<br/><br/>(a)	& (b)  No Sir. Question does not arise.<br/><br/>(c) However, Government of India has already taken necessary steps to increase fodder production in the country by providing financial assistance to the States and <br/>UTs including drought affected States under Centrally Sponsored National <br/>Livestock Mission of Department of Animal Husbandry, Dairying and Fisheries (DADF) with a Sub Mission on Feed and Fodder Development for the following components.<br/> <br/><br/>S. N.	Name of the Components<br/>    1. 	Fodder Production from Non-forest wasteland/ rangeland/ grassland/ non-arable land<br/>    2.	Fodder production from Forest land<br/>    3. 	Fodder Seed Procurement/ Production  & Distribution<br/>    4.	Introduction of Hand Driven Chaff-Cutter<br/>5.	Introduction of Power Driven Chaff-Cutter<br/>6.	Distribution of low capacity, tractor mountable Fodder Block Making units, hay baling machines/reapers/forage harvesters<br/>7.	Establishment of silage making Units<br/>8.	Establishment of by-pass protein production units<br/>9.	Establishment of Area Specific Mineral Mixture / Feed Pelleting/ Feed Manufacturing Unit.<br/>10.	Establishment/modernization of  Feed Testing Laboratories<br/><br/>From 2014-15 for drought affected areas, Additional Fodder Development Programme under Rashtriya Krishi Vikas Yojana (RKVY) of Department of Agriculture, Co-operation and Farmers Welfare has been formulated, which is continuing at present. Further, in addition to this, financial assistance is also provided which is supported by Department of Animal Husbandry, Dairying and Fisheries under RKVY for other fodder developmental activities planned by the States.<br/><br/>*******<br/>

records.qtitle: Implementation of PMAGY
records.name: Renuka Chowdhury
records.qn_text: (a) whether the SC component in the Pradhan Mantri Aadarsh Gram Yojana (PMAGY) has not been properly implemented in certain States; <br/><br/>(b) if so, the details thereof, along with the reasons therefor; and <br/><br/>(c) the corrective steps taken by Government in the matter?<br/>
records.ans_text: MINISTER OF STATE FOR SOCIAL JUSTICE AND EMPOWERMENT<br/>(SHRI VIJAY SAMPLA)<br/><br/>(a): Pradhan Mantri Adrash Gram Yojana (PMAGY) is implemented for the integrated development of villages having Scheduled Caste (SC) population of more than 50%. The Scheme does not have a separate SC component as it is intended for their overall benefit.<br/><br/>(b) & (c): In view of (a) above, does not arise.<br/>

records.qtitle: Illegal export of thorium rich sand from Tamil Nadu
records.name: Renuka Chowdhury
records.qn_text: <br/>(a)whether Government has seen the recent media reports  regarding large scale illegal export of thorium rich sand from Tamil  Nadu to China  and Europe via Sri Lanka,if so, the details thereof;<br/><br/>(b)the preventive steps taken by the Government in the matter; and<br/><br/>(c)the outcome of the vigilance probe about illegal sand smuggling and the nexus between a private group and a section of Indian Rare Earth Limited (IRE)  <br/>management in this regard?<br/><br/>
records.ans_text: <br/>THE MINISTER OF STATE FOR PERSONNEL, PUBLIC GRIEVANCES & PENSIONS AND PRIME MINISTER’S OFFICE (DR. JITENDRA SINGH):<br/><br/>(a)Yes, Sir. Recently, there have been some media reports that private companies have been allowed to export monazite of millions of tonnes, and that India has lost large quantities of thorium of value worth lakhs of crores of rupees.  The report alleges that Thorium resources, which are found in the beach sand minerals in the coastal areas of the country, which  are being allowed to be indiscriminately exported abroad on a large-scale, depriving the country of these resources in the long run.  The media reports are a large number of conjectures, baseless presumptions and some outright inaccuracies and fallacies.    <br/><br/>The coastal region of peninsular India contains economically important minerals such as garnet, ilmenite, leucoxene, monazite, rutile, sillimanite and zircon commonly known as beach sand minerals. Of these, monazite is defined as a ‘prescribed substance’ under the Atomic Energy Act, 1962 (AE Act) as amended in 2006(Notified in the Gazette of India (57), dated January 20, 2006).Atomic Minerals Directorate for Exploration and Research (AMD) of the Department of Atomic Energy (DAE) has carried out extensive surveys along the coastal region of the country to assess the distribution of beach sand minerals, including monazite. A license from the Department of Atomic Energy (DAE) under the Atomic Energy (Working of the Mines, Minerals and Handling of Prescribed Substances) Rules 1984 promulgated under the Atomic Energy Act 1962 is necessary for exporting monazite. Violation of this provision is a cognizable offence under the Code of Criminal Procedure and is punishable with imprisonment for a term, which may extend to five years or with fine or with both. DAE has not issued any license to any private entity either for production of monazite, or for its downstream processing for extracting thorium, or the export of either monazite or thorium. Export of the beach sand minerals (not monazite), falls under Open General License and does not require any authorization from DAE. <br/><br/>Since the other beach sand minerals and monazite (which contains thorium) occur together, companies handling beach sand minerals have to get a license under the Atomic Energy (Radiation Protection) Rules 2004 from the Atomic Energy Regulatory Board (AERB). As per the licensing conditions, the licensee, after separating the beach sand minerals has to dispose of the tailings, which contain monazite, within its company premises or as backfill, depending on the monazite content. These institutions are under strict regulatory control. They send quarterly reports to AERB stating the amount of tailings disposed of safely either in the premises or as backfill. Inspectors from AERB survey these areas to ensure that the licensing conditions are met. Export of monazite without a license from AERB is a violation of the Atomic Energy (Radiation Protection) Rules 2004. <br/><br/>Indian Rare Earths Limited (IREL), a wholly owned Public Sector Undertaking of the Government of India (GOI) under DAE, is the only entity which has been permitted to produce and process monazite, and handle it for domestic use as well as for export. <br/>	<br/>Apart from thorium, monazite contains rare earths too. On account of its radio-activity and other characteristics, extracting rare earths from monazite is commercially not attractive, unless mixed rare earths are separated as a by-product following extraction of thorium. The annual requirement of thorium-oxide for the 300 MWe Indian Advanced Heavy Water Reactor will be about five tons, with a one-time requirement of less than sixty tons  for the initial core. <br/><br/>The information available in IAEA documents, about the national nuclear programmes of different countries, does not give any indication that any country, other than India, is planning significant use of thorium either in the reactors currently under operation or in those being considered for deployment in the near future. Hence, it is unlikely that there is a demand overseas for large amounts of thorium.  In view of the above, the media reports, alleging illegal exports of huge quantities of thorium out of the country are not based on facts.<br/><br/>(b) & (c) Does not arise in view of the reply at (a) above	<br/><br/>*****<br/>

records.qtitle: High incidence of sickle cell anaemia
records.name: Renuka Chowdhury
records.qn_text: (a)	whether Government is aware that incidence of disease of sickle cell anaemia is very high among tribal communities in Scheduled Areas of the country;<br/><br/>(b)    	if so, the details thereof; and <br/><br/>(c)	 the steps taken by Government to redesign primary and health services in Scheduled Areas in order to meet the challenge?<br/><br/>
records.ans_text: MINISTER OF STATE FOR TRIBAL AFFAIRS<br/>(SHRI MANSUKHBHAI DHANJIBHAI VASAVA)<br/><br/>(a) to (c) : The prevalence of Sickle Cell Anemia is higher in the tribal belt of Western,Central and Southern IndianStates having Schedule V Areas; not so much in the tribes of North-East India including Schedule VI areas. A statement showing result of screening process for determining incidences of Sickle Cell Trait / Disease among ST persons in the States having Schedule V areas is at Annexure. <br/><br/>There is a little worthwhile treatment for the disease as of now but with management of disease, severity and complications can be curtailed to improve the quality of life and life span. The sickle cell gene is passed from generation to generation in a pattern of inheritance. Government has decided to screen three crore tribal children across the country to find the severity of incidences of Sickle Cell Anemia among them. The children with Sickle Cell trait or disease are counselled through their parents not to marry the other carrying trait or disease in order to control spread of the disease to next generation. The Ministry organized regional training workshops in collaboration with Indian Council of Medical Research (ICMR) to facilitate State/ UTs to train adequate manpower to undertake the screening exercise using a simple and cost effective screening test developed by ICMR. In addition, Department of Biotechnology is involved in research to find cure of the disease. <br/><br/>****<br/>

records.qtitle: Integrated Check Posts at Hili and Changrabandha in West Bengal
records.name: Renuka Chowdhury
records.qn_text: (a) whether Government has decided to set up Integrated Check Posts (ICPs) at Hili and Changrabandha on Indo-Bangladesh border in West Bengal;<br/><br/>(b) if so, the present status thereof; and<br/><br/>(c) the time by which these ICPs are likely to be operational?<br/>
records.ans_text: MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HOME AFFAIRS<br/>(SHRI KIREN RIJIJU)<br/><br/><br/>(a) to (c):	Hili and Changrabandha are among the 13 locations identified for setting up of Integrated Check Posts (ICPs) in the next phase.  The land acquisition for both these ICPs is under process.   The completion of these ICPs would depend upon the transfer of land by the State Government to the Land Ports Authority of India (LPAI).<br/><br/>********<br/>

records.qtitle: Poor state of CGHS dispensary, Janakpuri, New Delhi
records.name: Renuka Chowdhury
records.qn_text: Will the Minister of HEALTH AND FAMILY WELFARE be pleased to state: <br/><br/>(a) whether Government is aware of bad state of functioning of CGHS Dispensary (61) in Janakpuri, New Delhi due to malfunctioning of server, absence of doctors and non-availability of medicines daily; <br/><br/>(b) if so, the reasons therefor; and <br/><br/>(c) the fresh steps taken by Government to ensure proper functioning of the dispensary in order to avoid unavoidable inconvenience to the CGHS beneficiaries, most of whom are aged and retired from service?<br/><br/>
records.ans_text: THE MINISTER OF STATE FOR HEALTH AND FAMILY WELFARE <br/>(SHRI SHRIPAD YESSO NAIK)<br/><br/><br/>(a) to (c):  A statement is laid on the Table of the House<br/> <br/>STATEMENT REFERRED TO IN REPLY TO RAJYA SABHA<br/>STARRED QUESTION NO. 176* FOR 10TH MAY, 2016<br/><br/><br/>(a)	&	(b):  There is no shortage of doctors or regular shortage of medicines at CGHS Wellness Centre in Janakpuri. However, there was internet connectivity problem during the period between 9th April 2016 to 15th April 2016 due to which the medicines had to be issued manually causing some inconvenience to the beneficiaries. <br/><br/>(c):   The following steps have been taken to ensure proper functioning of the dispensary:<br/>(i)  Aadhar based bio-metric attendance system has been installed to monitor the punctuality.  <br/>(ii) Specialists/GDMOs with specialist qualification are working in the polyclinic and geriatric centre to provide ease in specialist consultation to CGHS beneficiaries.  <br/>(iii) There is a separate queue for senior citizens/pensioners at registration counter and pharmacy counter in the CGHS Wellness Centres.<br/>(iv)	Senior Citizens/pensioners can consult CMO i/c without standing in queue.<br/>

records.qtitle: Depletion in fleet strength of AAC
records.name: Renuka Chowdhury
records.qn_text: (a) whether it is a fact that the Army Aviation Corps (AAC) is plagued with 32 per cent deficiency in its authorised fleet strength, if so, the details thereof;<br/><br/>(b) the reasons for failure of Government to replace the 30 years old Chetak helicopter fleet;<br/><br/>(c) the number of military helicopters crashed during the last three years along with casualties; and<br/><br/>(d) the corrective steps taken by Government in this regard?<br/>
records.ans_text: MINISTER OF DEFENCE<br/>SHRI MANOHAR PARRIKAR<br/><br/>(a) & (b): The present holding of helicopters in Army Aviation Corps (AAC) is 73 percent of the authorized strength.  An Inter Government Agreement has been signed in 2015 with Russian Government for procurement of 200 Kamov helicopters for replacing Chetak / Cheetah fleet.<br/><br/>(c) & (d): Details of Army helicopters crashed during last three years along with casualities are as under:-<br/><br/>Year	No. of Army Helicopter Crashed	Casualty<br/><br/>2013	01	--<br/>2014	02	03<br/>2015	03	02<br/><br/>All crashes are investigated by a Court of Inquiry to find out the cause of accidents and to recommend remedial measures to prevent accidents.  Remedial measures suggested by the Court of Inquiry are implemented at various levels.  Standard Operating Procedures are constantly reviewed and stringent training norms are followed to minimized accidents.  Detailed analysis of cause factors of the accidents in the form of ‘Accident / Incident Compendium’ are published regularly for spreading awareness.  Regular interactions are also carried out with the Original Equipment Manufacturers to implement technical upgradations and modifications as recommended from time to time.<br/><br/>******<br/>

records.qtitle: Inadequate repair facilities for Sukhoi fleet
records.name: Renuka Chowdhury
records.qn_text: (a) whether it is a fact that our Sukhoi fleet suffers from high rate of AOG (Aircraft on Ground since not airworthy);<br/><br/>(b) if so, the details thereof along with the reasons for lack of spares and non-availability of adequate repair facilities; and<br/><br/>(c) the remedial steps taken by Government in this regard?<br/>
records.ans_text: MINISTER OF DEFENCE<br/>           SHRI MANOHAR PARRIKAR<br/><br/>(a)  Aircraft on Ground (AOG) in Sukhoi fleet are within the permissible limit of 10%.  The AOGs are kept within permissible limit by regular procurement of spares and undertaking timely repairs at the facilities set up at HAL Divisions and through long term repair agreements with the Russian Original Equipment Manufacturers.<br/><br/>(b) & (c):  Do not arise.<br/><br/><br/>*******<br/>

records.qtitle: Environmental flow in rivers
records.name: Renuka Chowdhury
records.min_name: WATER RESOURCES, RIVER DEVELOPMENT AND GANGA REJUVENATION
records.qn_text: (a) whether the environmental flows in all rivers and tributaries of Ganga river system are maintained round the year; <br/>(b) if so, the details thereof; <br/>(c) if not, the reasons therefor; and <br/>(d) the corrective steps taken by Government in this regard in order to fulfill their geological, ecological, socioeconomical and cultural functions with consensus of all affected people?<br/>
records.ans_text: THE MINISTER OF STATE FOR WATER RESOURCES, RIVER DEVELOPMENT AND GANGA REJUVENATION <br/>(PROF.  SANWAR  LAL  JAT)<br/><br/>(a)  No, Sir. The environmental flows in all rivers and tributaries of Ganga river system are not maintained. Central Water Commission (CWC) has informed that the Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change (MOEF & CC) decides the environmental flows to be released from the river valley projects to meet the ecological needs of the river. Accordingly the project authorities are advised for the release of the same. <br/>(b)  Does not arise.<br/>(c)  The main reasons for not maintaining the environmental flow are: (i) The geographical location of the river system, (ii) The unpredictable nature of the monsoon rainfall which is sometimes very weak and (iii) man-made reasons such as diverting water from the rivers for agricultural, industrial and other uses.<br/>However, one of the action points in the 7 identified thrust areas of Namami Gange programme is maintaining Aviral Dhara i.e. taking up comprehensive measures to determine and maintain environmental flow which is site, season and river specific and ensuring longitudinal connectivity.<br/> (d)    The Environment flow studies are an integral part of project specific Environment Impact Assessment (EIA) study. Ministry of Environment, Forest & Climate Change (MOEF&CC) conducts these studies. The environment flow to be released from river valley projects are finalized based on these studies.  MOEF&CC  conducts these studies.<br/>*****<br/>

records.qtitle: Conservation of Great Indian Bustard
records.name: Renuka Chowdhury
records.qn_text: (a)	whether Government is aware that the population of Great Indian Bustard has plummeted to less than 200 now in the country;<br/>(b)	if so, the details thereof along with the reasons therefor; and<br/>(c)	the steps taken by Government for conservation of this critically endangered species on the red list of International Union for Conservation of Nature (IUCN)?<br/>
records.ans_text: MINISTER OF STATE (INDEPENDENT CHARGE) FOR ENVIRONMENT, FOREST AND CLIMATE CHANGE <br/><br/>(SHRI PRAKASH JAVADEKAR)<br/><br/>(a)&(b)	 Population of Great Indian Bustard is known to have decreased to less than 300 in the country. This species is one of the critically endangered species of bird in India and is confined to 6 states viz., Rajasthan, Gujarat, Maharashtra, Madhya Pradesh, Karnataka and Andhra Pradesh. The population of this species is declining due to land use change in important bustard habitats which are grasslands.  <br/>	The Great Indian Bustard has been included in Schedule-I of the Wildlife (Protection) Act, 1972.  Thus, the species is getting utmost protection and conservation status in India. This species has also been identified as one of the species under the component ‘Recovery programmes for saving critically endangered species and habitats’ of the Centrally Sponsored Scheme of ‘Integrated Development of Wildlife Habitats’. Financial assistance is provided to the State Governments for protection of Great Indian Bustard habitats under the Centrally Sponsored Scheme of ‘Integrated Development of Wildlife Habitats’.  In the year 2015-16, central assistance of Rs.65.36 lakh  to Rajasthan, an amount of Rs. 11.79 lakh to Kutchh Bustard Sanctuary and Rs. 2.48 lakh to Gaga Great Indian Bustard Sanctuary of  Gujarat  and Rs.110.63 lakh to Maharashtra was provided for conservation of  Great Indian Bustards. <br/><br/>Under a programme for conservation breeding of Great Indian Bustard for augmenting wild population, Ministry has approved Rs.33.85 crores for five years. This programme will be implemented by Wildlife Institute of India in the State of Rajasthan, Gujarat and Maharashtra to begin with.  <br/><br/>***<br/><br/><br/><br/><br/><br/><br/>

records.qtitle: Cultivation of new arhar variety
records.name: Renuka Chowdhury
records.qn_text: (a)	whether scientists of Indian Agricultural Research Institute have developed a new arhar variety – pigeon pea that matures in 120 days;<br/><br/>(b)	if so, the details thereof, along with its main features; and<br/><br/>(c)	the time by which the new variety of arhar is likely to be made available to farmers for commercial cultivation?<br/>
records.ans_text: MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF AGRICULTURE AND FARMERS WELFARE (DR. SANJEEV KUMAR BALYAN)<br/><br/>(a) & (b):	Indian Agricultural Research Institute has developed early maturing (120 days) arhar genotype.  This genotype is of determinate habit, short statured (<100 cm), suited for close planting (30x15 cm) and amenable to mechanical harvesting.  <br/><br/>(c)	This genotype is yet to be evaluated in different agro-ecologies in All India Coordinated Research Project (AICRP) on Pigeonpea.<br/><br/>******<br/>

records.qtitle: Pest attack on CR 1009 Samba rice variety
records.name: Renuka Chowdhury
records.qn_text: (a)	whether Government is aware that CR-1009 Samba rice variety, grown widely in Delta region, has over the years become susceptible to pests such as brown plant hopper and bacterial blight;<br/><br/>(b)	if so, the details thereof, along with the yield losses reported due to such pest attack; and<br/><br/>(c)	the corrective steps taken by Government to develop new pest resistant variety of Samba rice for Delta region in order to prevent high scale losses to Samba cultivator farmers of the region?<br/>
records.ans_text: MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF AGRICULTURE AND FARMERS WELFARE (DR. SANJEEV KUMAR BALYAN)<br/><br/>(a)	Mono culturing of few selected rice varieties repeatedly for many years results in loss of resistance/tolerance of the rice variety against pest and diseases.  CR 1009 was released more than two decades back and the same, though still popular, grown widely in the delta region, had over the years become susceptible to pests such as Brown Plant Hopper (BPH) and Bacterial (Yield) Blight among other pests.  It is not unusual that due to continuous pest pressure the tolerance level is reduced.  To meet the challenge, ICAR Institutes and State Agricultural Universities are continuously engaged in breeding varieties and improving existing varieties to withstand the onslaught of pests and diseases.<br/><br/>(b)	Yield losses in Samba rice variety depends on the intensity and spread of the disease (BLB) and the insect pest (BPH).<br/><br/>	Moderate to severe incidence of bacterial blight of rice (Xanthomonas oryzae pv. Oryzae) was recorded on rice variety CR 1009 (Savitri) with an average yield loss of 15-20% in areas like Kariakal in Puduchhery and Thanjavur in Tamil Nadu recently.<br/><br/><br/>(c)	ICAR-Indian Institute of Rice Research (IIRR), Hyderabad in collaboration with Centre for Cellular and Molecular Biology (CCMB) have introgressed three major Bacterial Blight resistance genes, Xa21, xa13 and xa5 into the genetic background of Samba Mahsuri.  Resulting improved Samba Mahsuri is released in the states of Tamil Nadu, Karnataka, Telangana and Andhra Pradesh.  The variety is being promoted aggressively by Indian Institute of Rice Research and National Rice Research Institute in the pest endemic areas.<br/><br/>	A new rice cultivar AD 09367 is also developed for cultivation in the Delta region.  The new variety has high tolerance to major pests and diseases, with yield advantage of 10 per cent over CR 1009.<br/><br/>******<br/>

records.qtitle: Amending the Juvenile Justice (Care and Protection of Children) Act, 2000
records.name: Renuka Chowdhury
records.qn_text: (a)	whether there is no provision in Juvenile Justice (Care and Protection of Children) Act, 2000 about vicious, unregenerate and convicted juvenile, who despite having undergone the reformation process for maximum penalty continue to be a menace to society, if so, the details thereof, and ;<br/>(b)	the steps taken by Government to plug the loopholes in the Act?<br/>
records.ans_text: MINISTER OF WOMEN AND CHILD DEVELOPMENT<br/>(SHRIMATI MANEKA SANJAY GANDHI)<br/><br/>(a) & (b):	The Government has recently enacted the Juvenile Justice (Care and Protection of Children) Act, 2015 (JJ Act, 2015) repealing the Juvenile Justice (Care and Protection of Children) Act, 2000 to overcome the problems that were faced in the implementation of the JJ Act, 2000. The JJ Act, 2015 has came into effect from         15th January, 2016. Amongst the various provisions of the JJ Act, 2015 there are special provisions to deal with children in the age group of 16-18 years who commit heinous offences which will act as deterrent, for such children.<br/><br/>********<br/> <br/>

records.qtitle: Comprehensive policy on MSME
records.name: Renuka Chowdhury
records.qn_text: (a)	 whether there is no integrated approach for development of MSMEs despite the fact that the sector accounts for large scale manufacturing and export;<br/><br/>(b)	if so , the details thereof, along with the reasons therefor; and<br/><br/>(c)	the steps taken by Government to integrate various policies pertaining to MSME sector and whether Government would come out with a comprehensive policy?<br/>
records.ans_text: MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF<br/>MICRO, SMALL AND MEDIUM ENTERPRISES<br/>(SHRI GIRIRAJ SINGH)<br/><br/><br/>(a) to (c): 	The schemes and programmes of the Ministry of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises have been designed to address the issues related to credit, marketing, technology, skill and infrastructure required by MSMEs.  Though each thematic scheme has its own unique structures and components, they generally compliment each other and promote the common objective of development of MSMEs.  As the components of MSME policy are dispersed across Departments and Ministries, a need has been felt to frame a comprehensive policy. Accordingly, one man Committee has been constituted by the Government to recommend a comprehensive policy for MSMEs.<br/>

records.qtitle: Steel plant in Khammam district of Telangana
records.name: Renuka Chowdhury
records.qn_text: (a)	whether the Andhra Pradesh Reorganization Act, 2014 provides for setting up of a steel plant by SAIL in Khammam district of Telangana;<br/><br/>(b)	if so, the present status in this regard;<br/><br/>(c)	the reasons for inordinate delay in setting up of the steel plant; and<br/><br/>(d)	the immediate steps taken by Government to fulfil the promise made in this regard in an Act passed by the Parliament?<br/>
records.ans_text: THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF	       (SHRI VISHNU DEO SAI)<br/>STEEL AND MINES<br/><br/>(a)to(d): In terms of the Thirteenth Schedule of the Andhra Pradesh Reorganization Act, 2014, SAIL was to examine within six months from the appointed day i.e. 02.06.2014, the feasibility of establishing an integrated steel plant in the Khammam District of Telangana. A feasibility report was submitted by SAIL to the Government on 02.12.2014. Thus, SAIL has completed the task assigned to it as per the Andhra Pradesh Reorganization Act, 2014. As per the report, the feasibility of setting up of Steel Plant with the given configurations is prima facie not financially viable. In view of this, a Task Force comprising of representatives from the Central & State Government, SAIL, RINL and NMDC was constituted on 06.02.2015 to suggest ways and means to make the project financially viable.<br/><br/>********<br/><br/>

records.qtitle: Issue of multi city, multiple entry visa to businessmen of SAARC countries
records.name: Renuka Chowdhury
records.qn_text: (a) whether Government had decided to issue multi-city, multiple-entry business visa to businessmen of SAARC countries including Pakistan;<br/><br/>(b) if so, the details thereof, and<br/><br/>(c) the precautionary steps taken by Government to check the entry of terrorists in the garb of businessmen?<br/>
records.ans_text: MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HOME AFFAIRS<br/>(SHRI KIREN RIJIJU)<br/><br/>(a)  to (c):	As per extant instructions, multiple entry Business visa can be granted for a period up to 5 years or for a shorter duration as per the requirement to nationals of SAARC countries except in the case of nationals of Nepal, Bhutan and Pakistan. Citizens of Nepal and Bhutan do not require any visa for visiting India. Further, city specific visas are issued only in the case of Pakistan nationals. A scheme for grant of Business visa up to 3 years to Pakistan nationals has been introduced in July, 2015. Under this scheme, Pakistani businessmen of assured<br/>...2/-<br/><br/>-2-<br/>RS.US.Q.No.  1211 FOR 04.05.2016<br/> financial standing and credentials and who meet the following eligibility criteria can be granted Business visa for a period up to 3 years with multiple entry facility :- <br/><br/>	(1) 	In the case of those who had earlier been given 1-year Business visa with the prior approval of the Ministry of Home Affairs, the total value of imports and exports (of goods and services) of the firm/company/business establishment for which the Pakistani national is working should exceed Rs. 50 lakhs in the preceding financial year.<br/><br/>	(2) 	In the case of those not covered by (1) above, the total value of imports and exports (of goods and services) of the firm/company/business establishment for which the Pakistani  national is working should exceed Rs. 1 crore in the preceding financial year. Further, such Pakistani national should be a member of any National Chambers of Commerce of Pakistan/ SAARC Chamber of Commerce and Industry or is accredited with or certified by any National Chambers of Commerce and Industry in India. <br/><br/>	(3) 	This type of visa will be issued only to those Pakistani <br/>...3/-<br/>-3-<br/>RS.US.Q.No. 1211 FOR 04.05.2016<br/>nationals whose annual income is not less than Pak Rs. 10 lakhs. <br/><br/>The period of stay during each visit by Pakistani nationals granted this type of visa shall not exceed 30 days and they will be exempted from Police Reporting. Number of places of visit will be restricted to 15.<br/><br/>The scheme provides for stringent conditions for grant of Business visa up to 3 years for Pakistani Businessmen. The visa will be granted only after prior clearance of the Ministry of Home Affairs. <br/><br/>However, the High Commissioner of India in Islamabad has been given powers to grant such Business Visa, in rare and exceptional cases, to well known business persons fulfilling the eligibility criteria. In such cases visa shall be granted only after the visa applications are uploaded on the online visa application system and the details of visas issued shall also be uploaded immediately, which will be accessible to the security agencies in India. <br/>*****<br/>

records.qtitle: Infiltration on Indo Bangladesh border through riverine border
records.name: Renuka Chowdhury
records.qn_text: a) whether Government is aware of large scale infiltration on Indo-Bangladesh border using boats through the riverine border;<br/><br/>(b) if so, the details thereof, along with the number of cases of infiltration through riverine border came to the notice of Government during last three years, year-wise; and<br/><br/>(c) the fresh steps taken by Government to stop infiltration from Bangladesh using boats through riverine border?<br/>
records.ans_text: MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HOME AFFAIRS<br/>(SHRI KIREN RIJIJU)<br/><br/>(a) & (b):	No large scale infiltration on Indo-Bangladesh border using boats through the riverine border has come to notice of Border Security Force (BSF).<br/><br/>(c):	The riverine areas of all the borders are patrolled by the Border Security  Forces (BSF)  with the help of Floating Border Out Posts (FBOPs), <br/>….2/<br/><br/>-2-<br/>R.S.US.Q.NO.1176 FOR 04.05.2016<br/>mechanized boats, speed boats, medium crafts etc. as per the availability.  The Hi-Tech surveillance equipments along with day and night vision devices are also used for domination of riverine border areas.  Further, to enhance surveillance along riverine areas of the border, recently, Ministry of Home Affairs has ‘in-principle’ approved deployment of Technology Solutions in the riverine/low-lying stretches of the border in form of Sensors, Cameras, Optical Fiber Cables, Radars etc.<br/><br/>            ******<br/>

records.qtitle: Printing of defective currency notes
records.name: Renuka Chowdhury
records.qn_text: Will the Minister of FINANCE be pleased to state:<br/>(a)	whether it is a fact that thousands of ?500 and ?1000 defective notes printed at Security Paper Mill, Hoshangabad have hit the market in the recent past;<br/>(b)	if so, the details thereof, along with the reasons therefor; and<br/>(c)	the corrective steps taken by Government for hassle free replacement of such notes by the banks on being approached by the people?<br/>
records.ans_text: MINISTER OF STATE FOR FINANCE<br/>(SHRI JAYANT SINHA)<br/>(a) & (b): On December 11, 2015 it was informed by one of the Regional Offices of RBI that they had received some banknotes of ? 1000 denomination with inset letter ‘L’ belonging to some particular series without having Security thread.The incident happened in the Hosangabad Unit of the Security Printing and Minting Corporation of India Ltd (SPMCIL). Other essential features were present in the banknotes in question.The defective notes found to be in circulation amounted to ?7.56 Lakhs only.All the bank branches/currency chests & RBI offices were immediately instructed to stop issuing all banknotes of ?1000 denomination belonging to the detected series. Further they were advised to do detailed verification of these notes in stock. Instructions were issued to all the Concerned Regional Offices of RBI regarding detailed verification of stocks of notes as indicated by SPMCIL. However subsequently It was decided to remit back these notes to SPMCIL for thorough verification and resupply only those which are found to be fit for circulation.<br/>(c): These banknotes in question are genuine but printed defectively. Extant instructions are already in place to deal with such cases.<br/>

records.qtitle: Unused and rejected bombs at Ordnance Factory, Jabalpur
records.name: Renuka Chowdhury
records.qn_text: (a) whether thousands of unexploded and rejected bombs and Russian rejected RDX is lying in the premises of Ordnance Factory Khamarie (OFA) in Jabalpur, Madhya Pradesh, if so, the details thereof;<br/><br/>(b) whether Government has no policy to dispose these explosives and if not, the reasons therefor; and<br/><br/>(c) the steps taken by Government for safe disposal of these explosives in order to avoid any untoward incident in future?<br/>
records.ans_text: MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF DEFENCE<br/>(RAO INDERJIT SINGH)<br/><br/><br/>(a)  No, Sir.  There are no unexploded and rejected bombs and Russian rejected RDX lying in the premises of Ordnance Factory Khamaria (OFK) in Jabalpur.<br/><br/>(b) & (c):  Disposal of all rejected / waste ammunition / explosives is a regular process.  Government has a laid down procedure and disposal activities are being carried out on regular basis following General Safety Directives (GSD).  All explosives stores for disposal are known and accounted.  Ordnance Factory Khamaria is adopting safety norms for all activities.  It has sufficient number of Magazines which are designed and constructed strictly following Storage and Transportation of Explosive Committee (STEC) norms.  Moreover, multi-level safety audits at various levels are also carried out regularly.<br/><br/>*******<br/>

records.qtitle: AYUSH 82 anti diabetic drug
records.name: Renuka Chowdhury
records.qn_text: Will the Minister of AYURVEDA, YOGA & NATUROPATHY, UNANI, SIDDHA AND HOMOEOPATHY be pleased to state: <br/><br/>(a) whether the Central Council of Research of Ayurveda Sciences has developed an anti-diabetic drug, AYUSH- 82; <br/><br/>(b) if so, the details and salient features of the drug; and<br/><br/> (c) the steps taken by Government for early commercialisation of AYUSH-82 for prevention and management of diabetes in the country?<br/><br/>
records.ans_text: THE MINISTER OF STATE (IC) OF THE MINISTRY OF AYURVEDA,<br/>YOGA & NATUROPATHY, UNANI, SIDDHA AND HOMOEOPATHY<br/>(SHRI SHRIPAD YESSO NAIK)<br/>(a) & (b):   Yes. For the management of diabetes mellitus, the Central Council for Research in Ayurvedic Sciences(CCRAS) has developed a formulation namely, AYUSH-82 from   05 Ayurvedic medicinal plants. The trials of the drug has shown significant reduction in blood sugar level along with clinical improvement. No toxic effects were noted during the trial. <br/>(c ):	Council has initiated action to commercialize  AYUSH-82.  Till now  M/S, Dabur India Ltd, New Delhi; M/S Kudos Laboratory India Ltd., New Delhi; and M/S  LA Granade Herbs & Pharma  Ltd., New Delhi have been granted licenses for manufacturing AYUSH-82.<br/>

records.qtitle: Compliance with international standards for safety by vehicle manufacturers
records.name: Renuka Chowdhury
records.qn_text: (a) whether Government has made it mandatory for vehicle manufacturers especially cars for complying with best international standards for safety of drivers and passengers for new vehicles;<br/><br/>(b) if so, the details thereof along with the details of the state of the art automotive design and testing centres existing in the country for the purpose; and<br/><br/>(c) the steps taken by Government to formulate new norms for crash test, emissions and other safety equipments to ensure safer vehicles manufacturing in the country?<br/>
records.ans_text: THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF ROAD TRANSPORT AND HIGHWAYS<br/><br/>(SHRI PON. RADHAKRISHNAN)<br/><br/>(a) & (b)  Government has introduced several safety standards, which are very similar to international regulation. All such requirements are notified under Central Motor Vehicles Rules, 1989 (CMVRs) from time to time. The following are the latest requirements which are in-line with international standards. These standards are already notified effective from the dates indicated.<br/> Date of Implementation	Applicability	Standard and description	UN Equivalent Standards	Pertaining to<br/>1st Oct 2017	New car models, and LMV of GVW < 1500 kg	AIS 096 – Protection of driver with regards to steering column intrusion (speed of impact ~ 50 kmph)	UN ECE R12	Full Frontal Crash test<br/>	New car models –<br/>GVW < 2500 kg	AIS 098 – Protection of the drivers and passengers in the event of an offset frontal collision (Speed of impact – 56 kmph)	UN ECE R98	40% overlap offset frontal crash test<br/>	New Car models and LCV category vehicles (with respect to height of vehicles)	AIS 099 –Protection of the Occupants in the event of a Lateral Collision (Speed of impact – 50 kmph)	UN ECE R99	Test of Moving deformable barrier crash perpendicular into stationary vehicle<br/> <br/>1st Oct 2018	New car models –<br/>GVW < 2500 kg	AIS 100 – Protection of pedestrians and other vulnerable road users in the event of a collision with a car	GTR 9	Pedestrian body forms being impacted on the hood of the vehicle<br/>1st Oct 2019	All car models, and LMV of GVW < 1500 kg	AIS 096 – Protection of driver with regards to steering column intrusion (speed of impact ~ 50 kmph)	UN ECE R12	Full Frontal Crash test<br/>	All car models –<br/>GVW < 2500 kg	AIS 098 – Protection of the drivers and passengers in the event of an offset frontal collision (Speed of impact – 56 kmph)	UN ECE R98	40% overlap offset frontal crash test<br/>	All Car models and LCV models category vehicles (with respect to height of vehicles)	AIS 099 –Protection of the Occupants in the event of a Lateral Collision (Speed of impact – 50 kmph)	UN ECE R99	Test of Moving deformable barrier crash perpendicular into stationary vehicle<br/>1st Oct 2020	All car models –<br/>GVW < 2500 kg	AIS 100 – Protection of pedestrians and other vulnerable road users in the event of a collision with a car	GTR 9	Pedestrian body forms being impacted on the hood of the vehicle<br/>The government, under the National Automotive Testing and R&D Infrastructure Project (NATRiP) initiative has taken up project to setup state of art testing centres at Pune (Automotive Research Association of India), Manesar (International Centre for Automotive Technology), and Chennai (Global Automotive Research Centre). Of these centres, Crash Test Centre at ARAI is already operational and facility at ICAT is in advance stage of completion. The centre at Chennai (GARC) is expected to be ready by next year.<br/>(c)    Cars being manufactured from the dates mentioned in the above table need to have compliance at the manufacturing stage. In addition, standards for Seat Belts and their Anchorages, Child Seats, Seats and their Anchorages are already mandated step by step since 2010.  Regarding Emission, the current notified requirement is Bharat Stage IV (BS IV). The Government has notified draft notification  GSR 187(E) dated 19.02.2016 to introduce Bharat Stage VI emission norms, skipping BS-V emission norms for all vehicles to be applicable all over the country by 1st April, 2020.<br/> <br/>	 <br/>*****<br/>

records.qtitle: Provision for safe crossing of NH 44 near Peddakunta, Telangana
records.name: Renuka Chowdhury
records.qn_text: (a) whether a large number of men from Peddakunta Tanda tribal hamlet on NH 44 linking Hyderabad and Bangalore in Mahabubnagar district of Telangana have died in road accidents during the last five years;<br/><br/>(b) if so, the details thereof along with the reasons for not providing any service road or a safe point for residents to cross the highway near the hamlet;<br/><br/>(c) the reasons for constructing an underpass far away from hamlet rendering it completely useless for residents; and<br/><br/>(d) the corrective steps taken by Government to help the villagers in crossing the highway safely and properly compensate all affected residents?<br/>
records.ans_text: THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF ROAD TRANSPORT AND HIGHWAYS<br/> (SHRI PON. RADHAKRISHNAN)<br/><br/>(a) and (b)  During the last 5 years, 4 fatal accidents have taken place near Peddakunta Tanda tribal hamlet as the villagers instead of using (Pedestrian Under Pass) PUP at Km 42/100 tried to cross the highway directly.<br/>A PUP of size 2.5 m x 3 m was provided near the village at Km.42/100 during construction of bypass in 2009 to facilitate crossing of highway by pedestrians, 2-wheelers, cars, autos, tractors etc. As the village is on newly constructed Shadnagar bypass, there is no habitation abutting the highway, hence service road is not necessitated.<br/><br/>(c)    The PUP is at Km.42/100, close to the village.<br/><br/>(d)    The details of the measures taken by Government are as under:-<br/><br/>1)	Short Term remedial measures like providing additional sign boards (speed limit boards, pedestrian crossing boards), providing thermoplastic bar marking, providing of illumination etc., have been taken. <br/>2)	The median opening has been closed permanently (to curb unauthorized access and wrong direction movement). <br/>3)	Solar power lighting has been provided from Village to PUP.<br/>4)	Several Counseling / Education programs were conducted by the Concessionaire, Sr. Safety Expert (Chief Engineer Retd.) from MoRT&H and NGO (Road Safety Club). <br/>5)	Entry & Exit ramps near the PUP are being provided.<br/><br/>*****<br/>

records.qtitle: Revision of standards for common effluent treatment plants
records.name: Renuka Chowdhury
records.qn_text: (a) whether Government has revised standards for common effluent treatment plants operating at various industrial clusters in the country;<br/>(b) 	if so, the details thereof; and<br/>(c) 	the time by which the new norms/standards are likely to be enforced for improving the quality of industrial discharge across the country?<br/>
records.ans_text: MINISTER OF STATE (INDEPENDENT CHARGE) FOR ENVIRONMENT, FOREST AND CLIMATE CHANGE <br/><br/>SHRI PRAKASH JAVADEKAR<br/><br/>(a)&(b)    The Ministry has notified the revised standards for Common Effluent Treatment Plants (CETPs) operating at various industrial clusters on 01.01.2016. As per the notified standards, State Pollution Control Boards / Pollution Control Committees (SPCBs / PCCs) are empowered to prescribe inlet effluent quality standards for General Parameters, Ammonical-Nitrogen and Heavy metals as per design of the Common Effluent Treatment Plant (CETP) and local needs and conditions. The maximum allowable concentrations in treated effluent are specified in respect of Bio-chemical Oxygen Demand (BOD), Chemical Oxygen Demand (COD), Fixed Dissolved Solids (FDS) and Heavy Metals among other parameters considering three modes of disposal viz. ‘Discharge into sea’, ‘Discharge into Inland surface water’ and ‘Discharge on to land for irrigation’.<br/><br/>The ‘Discharge into sea’ (marine outfall) providing minimum dilution of 100 times at the point of discharge and 1500 times at a point 100 m away from discharge is considered for relaxed maximum permissible concentration of COD up to 500 milligram per liter. The maximum permissible FDS contribution by constituent units of a Common Effluent Treatment Plant (CETP) is permitted up to 1000 milligram per liter. For FDS concentration in excess of 1100 milligram per liter in raw water, SPCBs / PCCs are empowered to modify the FDS limit in treated effluent. 	In case of discharge of treated effluent on land for irrigation, provision has been made for monitoring the impact on soil and groundwater quality twice a year (pre-monsoon and post-monsoon) by Common Effluent Treatment Plants (CETP) management. The SPCBs / PCCs are also empowered to prescribe mixing ratio of treated effluent and sewage for disposal on to land for irrigation.<br/>	<br/>(c)    The revised standards are effective with effect from 01.01.2016.<br/><br/><br/>*****<br/>

records.qtitle: Setting up of new Horticultural University in Telangana
records.name: Renuka Chowdhury
records.qn_text: (a)	whether Government has decided to set up a new Horticultural University in Telangana;<br/><br/>(b)	if so, the present status of the proposal; and<br/><br/>(c)	the time by which the work on the project is likely to be taken up?<br/>
records.ans_text: THE MINISTER OF AGRICULTURE & FARMERS WELFARE<br/>(SHRI RADHA MOHAN SINGH)<br/><br/><br/>(a) to (c): 	A Statement is laid on the table of the House.<br/><br/>******<br/><br/>STATEMENT IN RESPECT OF PARTS (a) to (c) OF RAJYA SABHA STARRED QUESTION NO. 65 TO BE ANSWERED ON 29.04.2016 REGARDING “SETTING UP OF NEW HORTICULTURAL UNIVERSITY IN TELANGANA”<br/>________________________________________<br/><br/>(a)	Yes, Sir. During the Budget presentation in the Lok Sabha in the year 2014-15, Hon’ble Finance Minister, Government of India announced establishment of Horticultural University in Telangana. As per the budget announcement, financial support has been extended for State Horticultural University in Telangana state.<br/><br/>(b) & (c):	A notification dated 22.12.2014 was issued by the Government of Telangana for establishment of Sri Konda Laxman Telangana State Horticultural University with Headquarters of Rajendranagar Campus, Hyderabad.  Subsequently, the Government of Telangana on 29.09.2014 communicated that an area of about 500 ha has been identified at Mulugu, Medak District in Telangana State.  The Department of Agricultural Research and Education has already released Rs.10.00 crore during financial year 2014-15, and Rs.74.99 crores during financial year    2015-16 to the Telangana State University.  Further, an allocation of Rs.50.00 crore has been made in the Budget Estimates (BE) for the year 2016-17.<br/><br/>******<br/>

records.qtitle: Bomb disposal and detection squad for Railway Protection Force
records.name: Renuka Chowdhury
records.qn_text: (a)	whether the Railway Protection Force (RPF) does not have its own bomb disposal and detection squad;<br/><br/>(b)	if so, the details thereof along with the reasons therefor;<br/><br/>(c)	the reasons for supply of only a few items of bomb disposal and detection kit to RPF during the last five years and that too being lying idle and have expired; and<br/><br/>(d)	the corrective steps taken by Government to supply complete kit to RPF in order to prevent wastage of resources?<br/>
records.ans_text: MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF RAILWAYS<br/><br/>(SHRI MANOJ SINHA)<br/><br/>(a)	& (b): Prevention and detection of crime and maintenance of law and order over Railways is the statutory responsibility of States which is being discharged by them through the Government Railways Police (GRP). <br/><br/>To supplement efforts of GRP and to avert any mishap in station premises and trains, 278 sniffer dogs have been deployed by the Railway Protection Force (RPF) also for detection of explosive items over Indian Railway. Equipment like bomb basket, bomb suit, drilling machine, thermal cutter, telescopic prodder, non linear junction detector, under trolley search mirror, deep search metal detector,  etc. have been procured for handling of explosive substances over some zonal railways. <br/><br/><br/>(c) & (d): Strengthening and upgradation of security infrastructure is an ongoing process. Bomb detection and disposal system forms part of an Integrated Security System (ISS) that envisages strengthening surveillance mechanism at 202 sensitive stations over Indian Railways. Issues concerning availability of eligible vendors, specification, inspection of equipment, etc. were raised by some of the Zonal Railways. These issues have since been addressed and necessary action is being initiated by concerned zones for acquisition of items under ISS accordingly.<br/><br/>[[[[[[[<br/>**** <br/><br/><br/><br/><br/><br/><br/>

records.qtitle: Development of low erucic acid varieties of mustard
records.name: Renuka Chowdhury
records.qn_text: (a)	whether ICAR has developed a low erucic acid variety of mustard, if so, the details thereof; and<br/><br/>(b)	the steps taken by Government to make it available to farmers for large scale commercial cultivation at the earliest?<br/>
records.ans_text: MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF AGRICULTURE AND FARMERS WELFARE (DR. SANJEEV KUMAR BALYAN)<br/><br/>(a)	The All India Coordinated Research Project on Rapeseed-Mustard (AICRPRM) of Indian Council of Agricultural Research (ICAR) has developed eight low erucic acid varieties of Indian mustard namely Pusa Karishma, Pusa Mustard 21, Pusa Mustard 22, RLC-1, Pusa Mustard 24, RLC-2, Pusa Mustard 29 and Pusa Mustard 30.<br/><br/>(b)	About 2300 kg breeder seed of these improved varieties was provided to various public and private seed producing agencies during the last five years ending 2014-15, in order to make available their quality seed to the farmers for large scale cultivation.<br/><br/>	Besides, Pusa Mustard 30 variety has been licensed to three seed companies such as M/s Malwa Enterprises, Punjab; M/s Arpan Seeds Pvt Ltd., Rajasthan and Ajeet Seeds, Aurangabad for its multiplication and distribution among the farmers.<br/><br/>******<br/>

records.qtitle: Ex servicemen for physical training in schools
records.name: Renuka Chowdhury
records.qn_text: (a) whether Government is considering to utilize the services of ex-servicemen for providing physical training to students in school, if so, the details thereof; and<br/><br/>(b) the time by which the proposal is likely to be implemented all over the country?<br/>
records.ans_text: MINISTER OF HUMAN RESOURCE DEVELOPMENT<br/>(SMT. SMRITI ZUBIN IRANI)<br/><br/>(a) & (b). The Central Government is working on a pilot programme ‘Vidyanjali’ to involve people from Indian Diaspora, retired teachers, retired government officials including retired defence personnel, retired professionals and women who are home makers to volunteer to strengthen co-scholastic activities in schools such as reading.  These volunteers will not be a replacement for regular teachers and neither will they be involved in any kind of formal teaching. In an Education Minister’s meeting held on 08.02.2016, nineteen States/UTs had expressed willingness to participate in this programme. <br/><br/>*****<br/>

records.qtitle: Removal of contents from NCERT books
records.name: Renuka Chowdhury
records.qn_text: (a) whether it is a fact that contents about a large number of national leaders/freedom fighters/revolutionaries have been either removed or snipped/curtailed from NCERT text books; (b) if so, the details thereof along with the reasons therefor; and <br/><br/>(c) the corrective steps taken by Government in this regard?<br/>
records.ans_text: MINISTER OF HUMAN RESOURCE DEVELOPMENT<br/>(SMT. SMRITI ZUBIN IRANI)<br/><br/>(a)	There has been no change in the contents relating to national leaders, freedom fighters and revolutionaries, available in the National Council of Educational Research and Training (NCERT) textbooks, which have been in circulation since 2007-08.<br/><br/>(b) & (c)  Do not arise.<br/>

records.qtitle: International safety standards for new vehicles
records.name: Renuka Chowdhury
records.qn_text: (a) whether Government has made it mandatory for vehicle especially car manufacturers for complying with best international standards for safety of driver and passengers for new vehicles; (b) if so, the details thereof along with the details of state-of-the-art automotive design and testing centres existing in the country for the purpose; and <br/>(c) the steps taken by Government to  formulate new norms for crash test, emissions and other safety equipment to ensure safer vehicles manufacturing in the country?<br/>

records.qtitle: Theft reported in multi utility tunnel in Connaught Place, New Delhi
records.name: Renuka Chowdhury
records.qn_text: (a) the total number of cases of thefts reported in the 1.2 km. long multi-utility tunnel of NDMC in Connaught Place, New Delhi during last five years;<br/><br/>(b) whether Government is aware that poor security of this tunnel is a security threat for common people; and<br/><br/>(c) the concrete steps taken by Government in this regard and to ensure that all the vulnerable areas of the tunnel are sanitized on regular basis?<br/>
records.ans_text: MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HOME AFFAIRS<br/>(SHRI HARIBHAI PARATHIBHAI CHAUDHARY)<br/><br/>(a) to (c):	A Statement is laid on the Table of the House.<br/><br/>******<br/><br/><br/><br/><br/><br/><br/><br/><br/><br/>-2-<br/><br/>STATEMENT IN REPLY TO THE RAJYA SABHA STARRED QUESTION NO.*42 FOR 27.04.2016.<br/><br/>(a) to (c):	The Delhi Police has informed that 04 cases of theft have been reported from the multi-utility tunnel of NDMC in Connaught Place, New Delhi during the last five years. <br/>Delhi Police have deployed 01 Sub-Inspector, 01 Head Constable, 03 Constables, 01 Quick Reaction Team and 01 PCR Van in the area where this tunnel falls. <br/>********<br/>

records.qtitle: Development of city side infrastructure at regional airports
records.name: Renuka Chowdhury
records.qn_text: (a) whether the Airports Authority of India (AAI) plans to develop city-side infrastructure at certain regional airports;<br/><br/>(b) if so, the details thereof along with the regional airports identified for the purpose; and<br/><br/>(c) the time by when the work on this plan is likely to commence?
records.ans_text: MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF CIVIL AVIATION<br/>(Dr Mahesh Sharma)<br/><br/>(a) Airports Authority of India (AAI) has taken up the city side development works at existing airports in order to enhance the passenger facilitation and services.<br/><br/>(b) AAI has planned to take up city side development initially at 8 Airports (Lucknow, Raipur, Tirupati, Kolkata, Varanasi, Jaipur, Bhubaneshwar and Amritsar) in Phase-I. In Phase-II, 11 Airports (Gaya, Vizag, Chandigarh (Old), Bangalore (Old), Indore, Coimbatore, Trivandrum, Chennai, Hyderabad (Begumpet), Guwahati & Ahmedabad) shall be taken up for city side<br/>development.<br/><br/>(c) The city side development works of Airports in Phase-I is likely to be taken up in next one year. The Phase-II is likely to be taken up in 2018.<br/>

records.qtitle: Stricter emission norms for two wheelers
records.name: Renuka Chowdhury
records.qn_text: (a) whether two wheelers contribute significantly to air pollution in comparison to other vehicles;<br/><br/>(b) if so, the details thereof; and<br/><br/>(c) the steps taken by Government to implement stricter green norms for two wheelers at the earliest and also to apply BS-VI emission standards for two wheelers also?<br/>
records.ans_text: THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF ROAD TRANSPORT AND HIGHWAYS<br/><br/>(SHRI PON. RADHAKRISHNAN)<br/><br/>(a) & (b) No, Sir. Two wheelers are equipped with small engines, hence contribute less to air pollution in comparison to other vehicles. Further, from year 2010, 95% of two wheelers has become 4-Stroke which has contributed in reducing the pollution level.   <br/>(c)	    The Ministry of Road Transport and Highways has issued draft notification GSR 431(E) dated 4th July, 2014 mandating Bharat Stage IV emission norms for two wheelers manufactured on and after the 1st April, 2016 for new types of vehicle models and from the 1st April, 2017 for existing types of vehicle models. Draft notification GSR 187(E) dated 19.02.2016 mandating Bharat Stage VI emission norms for all vehicles to be applicable all over the country by 1st April, 2020 has also been issued. <br/>	 <br/>*****<br/>

records.ans_text: MINISTER OF STATE (INDEPENDENT CHARGE) FOR ENVIRONMENT, FOREST AND CLIMATE CHANGE<br/><br/>(SHRI PRAKASH JAVADEKAR)<br/><br/>(a) The Genetic Engineering Appraisal Committee (GEAC) in its meeting held on 5.2.2016 had directed the applicant (Centre for Genetic Manipulation of Crop Plants (CGMCP), University of Delhi, South Campus) to revise the BIOSAFETY DOSSIER  in respect of their  application for environmental release of transgenic mustard hybrid DMH- developed using barnase, barstar and bar genes.  The revised dossier has been forwarded to the Sub-committee of the GEAC constituted for the purpose of review and experts comments.As of now, no decision to commercially release GM mustard has been taken.<br/><br/>(b)Does not arise.<br/><br/>(c) No specific time frame can be indicated as the safety assessment of GM plant is highly technical and is a long drawn process involving extensive consultations with the relevant stakeholders before a final decision is taken.<br/><br/>*************<br/>

records.qtitle: Closure of tea gradens in West Bengal
records.name: Renuka Chowdhury
records.qn_text: (a)	whether a large number of tea gardens in West Bengal have been closed, abandoned or are non-functional;<br/>(b)	if so, the details thererof along with the reasons therefor; and<br/>(c)	the steps taken by Government to reopen the tea gardens of the region and ensure that non-functional or abandoned tea gardens function properly?<br/>
records.ans_text: THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF COMMERCE AND INDUSTRY(INDEPENDENT CHARGE)<br/>(SMT. NIRMALA SITHARAMAN) <br/>                                                             *****<br/><br/>(a) &(b):As per information available, six tea gardens in West Bengal are, at present, closedand seven tea gardens are not functioning properly. The closed gardens, namely Dheklapara, Bundapani, Dharanipur, Redbank, Surendranagar and Madhu are reported to be closed due to several reasons including, inter alia, poor yields, poor garden management, excessive reliance of owners on debt with negligible equity infusion and poor condition of the gardens and factories resulting in low tea quality and price realization.  <br/>The seven gardens, namely Birpara, Garganda, Lankapara, Tulsipara, Huntapara, Dhumchipara and Demdima are reported to be under stress as the gardens have defaulted in payment of workers’ dues in respect of P.F.
