records.qtitle: . DISCOVERY OF DIAMOND DEPOSITS BY GSI IN MADHYA PRADESH
records.name: Renuka Chowdhury
records.qn_text:
(a) whether the Geological Survey of India has recently discovered diamond deposits in Madhya Pradesh;

(b) if so, the details thereof; and

(c) the export potential of the diamonds?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STEEL AND MINSTER OF MINES (SHRI BIRENDRA PRASAD BAISHYA)

(a) Geological Survey of India (GSI) has not discovered any diamond deposits in Madhya Pradesh recently. However, GSI has in the past located a number of kimberlite bodies, a known source rock for diamond in Raipur and bastar districts.

(b) The details are as under:-

(i) Panna diamond belt, Panna, Chattarpur, Damoh and Sagar district.

(ii) pairi-Khariar-Singora areas in Raipur district.

(iii) Indravati-Sabri area in Baster district.

(iv) Kimberlittic Utramafic and Bariarpur, Panna district very few of the kimberlite bodies indentified so far are diamond bearing.

(c) The exploration is at a very preliminary stage and hence it is not possible to make any export potential.

records.qtitle: DECLINE IN DIVIDEND PAID BY PSUS
records.name: Renuka Chowdhury
records.qn_text:
(a) whether disinvestments Public Sector Undertakings will lead to a corresponding decline in the amount of dividends which they pay to Government annually;and

(b) the funds likely to be raised from PSUs disinvestments during 1997-98 and the estimated loss of revenue of Government on this count?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF INDUSTRY (SHRI MURASOLI MARAN0

(a) This would be so if the dividend percentages are constant,but the amounts may not decline or could even increase if the dividend percentages go up due to higher profits.

(b) An amount of Rs.4800 crores is estimated to be raised from disinvestment during 1997-98. The estimated revenue loss to the Govt. due to decline in dividend which the PSUs pay cannot be quantified as it depends on a number of variable factors.

records.qtitle: PROCESSING OF FRUITS AND VEGETABLES IN THE COUNTRY .
records.name: Renuka Chowdhury
records.qn_text:
(a) the quantity of fruits and vegetables produced in the country and the percentages thereof which is being processed:

(b) the shortcomings in the proper growth of the industry;and

(c) the steps proposed to be taken to encourage modernisation of food processing industry as it has failed to register the desired level of growth despite the country being the world`s largest producer of fruits and vegetables.
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE OF THE MINISTRY OF FOOD PROCESSING INDUSTRY (SHRI DILIP KUMAR RAY):

(a) Production of fruit and vegetable in the country is estimated to be around 100 million tonnes. Processing of fruits and vegetable has increased from 0.5%in 1988 to 1.8% in 1996 of the total production.

(b) And

(c) While there is a great potential for growth of the industry, the slow growth can be attributed to factors such as lack of post harvest processing infrastructure, inadequate linkage between the farmers and the processors, and lack of marketing efforts etc. Government has been talking various steps for development of the Food processing Industries including fruits and vegetable processing. which inter-alia includes Liberalised policies for investment including foreign investment,removel of restrictions thereon, providing fiscal concessions Ministry of the Food processing industries is also implementing various Plan Schemes under which financial assistance is provided to State Government Joint Sector/Cooperative Sector etc.

records.qtitle: WHEAT IMPORT FOR POOR .
records.name: Renuka Chowdhury
records.qn_text:
(a) whether more wheat import is need to make available foodgrains to the poor at reasonable rates as domestic farmers did not sell Rabi yield; and

(b) whether adequate godown arrangements has been made to stock the imported wheat?
records.ans_text:
THE MINISTER OF AGRICULTURE AND MINISTER OF FOOD AND MINISTER OF CIVIL SUPPLIES, CONSUMER AFFAIRS AND PUBLIC DISTRIBUTION (SHRI CHATURANAN MISHRA)

(a) Government have already decided to import upto 4.00 million tonnes of wheat during 1996-97 and country, and a quantity of 26.75 lakh tonnes has already been contracted for import. Government keep on reviewing the stock position of foodgrains in the Central Pool with reference to the production of foodgrains, procurement trend, requirement for the Public Distribution System/Other Welfare Schemes, Open market prices to ensure adequate availability if foodgrains in the country.

(b) Yes, Sir.

records.qtitle: ONSHORE PEARL IN VISHAKHAPATNAM DISTRICT .
records.name: Renuka Chowdhury
records.qn_text:
(a) whether co-friendly onshore marine pearl culture is on the threshold of commercial production in Vishskhapatnam district;

(b) if so, the details thereof; and

(c) the likely market for export of cultured pearls?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF ENVIRONMENT AND FORESTS (PROF. SAIFUDDIN SOZ.):

(a)and(b) Two integrated on-shore marine pearl culture projects with production capacity of 12 kg per annum each are being set up near Vishakhapatnam with technology developed by Central Marine Fisheries Research Institute. Trial production is expected by December, 1997.

(c) The market for cultured marine pearls is vast, as the present production is insufficient to meet the world`s demand. There is, thus, a potential for export of cultured pearls.

records.qtitle: SAVING ELECTRICITY BY USING COMPACT FLUORESCENT LAMPS .
records.name: Renuka Chowdhury
records.qn_text:
(a) whether it is a fact that surprise checks conducted recently in Kendriya Bhandar branches in Delhi have revealed that Basmati rice being sol there, was adulterated and of inferior quality;

(b) if so, the details thereof; and

(c) whether any enquiry has been conducted in this regard and if so, the findings thereof and the punishmented out of hose found guilty?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF PERSONNEL, PUBLIC GRIEVANCES AND PENSIONS AND MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF PARLIAMENTARY AFFAIRS (SHRI S. R. BALASUBRAMONIYAN)

(a) to (c) Kendriya Bhandar sells Basmati Rice of reputed brands in the packings of producers. Apart from this, Kendriya Bhandar has also been selling rice including Basmati type in its own packing of 1 kg. After buying it in bulk. The rice sold meets the specifications prescribed in the Prevention of Find Adulteration (PFA) Act, and the same is released for sale only after proper testing to meet the above specifications. No Basmati Rice has been found to be adulterated as per the PFA act, either an adultered as per the PFA act, either at the time of pre-testing of goods before releasing them for sale, or `on the shelf testing`. The rice in question was, however, good tested (by picking up samples from the shelf) with a view to finding the extent of Basmati grains therein. The percentage of Basmati grains as revealed during the tests carried out on two different date (24.2.97 and 29.4.97) was considered low. It was, therefore, decided to stop sale Basmati rice, procured from pen mark in bulk, in the packing of Kendriya Bhandar. No further enquiry in the Matter in therefore, called for. However, the sale of brands of Basmati Rice in packings of the producers to meet customer demand continues.

records.qtitle: BRAIN DRAIN FROM ISRO .
records.name: Renuka Chowdhury
records.qn_text:
(a) whether there has been a brain drain of a serious dimension from the Indian Space Research Organisation during the last five years;

(b) if so, the number of scientists who left the Organisation during this period, which they have gone;

(c) whether it has seriously affected the work schedule of this prestigious science institute of the country; and

(d) the steps taken to stop this brain drain from ISRO?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE OF THE MINISTRY OF PLANNING AND PROGRAMME IMPLEMENTATION AND MINISTER OF STATE OF HE MINISTRY OF SCIENCE AND TECHNOLOGY (SHRI YOGINDER K. ALAGH)

(a) and (b) Scientists/Engineers leaving Indian space research Organisation (ISRO) is not a totally new phenomenon as there have been resignations in the pat, too. However, in the recent past, there has been an increase in the number of persons leaving the organisation possibly for better prospectus, especialaly in certain disciplines like computers and telecommunications. As many as 530 Scientists/Engineers have left during the last five years and personal reasons have been cited for such resignations. The liberalisation of the economy since 1991-92 has provided them new employment opportunities in our country itself with high remuneration levels. The exact information in respect of persons who have gone abroad, is not available.

(b) The resignations of Scientists/engineers have so far not had any serious impact on the schedule of the Space Programme. However, occasions did arise whether schedule critical work had to slow down for a while in a few areas owing to a number of Scientists/Engineers leaving almost at the same time.

(c) Better housing facilities, further opportunities for academic and related activities including further studies, enhancement of interface between Scientist and industry are among the steps proposed.

records.qtitle: ROLE OF ONGC AND OIL IN THE NEW OIL EXPLORATION POLICY .

(c) whether they are to apart with precious data to the private parties for the blocks on which they have worked for long, at huge costs; and

(d) if so, the reasons thereof?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY PETROLEUM AND NATURAL GAS (SHRI T. R. BAALU)

(a) and (b) Under the New Exploration Licensing Policy (NELP), ONGC and OIL will have level playing filed vis-à-vis private companies. They will be eligible for the same fiscal and contract terms as available to other private companies including getting international price of oil under the new policy. Under the NELP, they will need to compete for obtaining petroleum exploration licenses.

(c) and (d) Under NELP, Government seeks to achieve through competition the most effective exploration efforts in the country. It is considered to be in public interest to share the available data on the offered areas with the eligible bidders in order to attract attract great investment flows in this critical sector. On the offered areas, if the ONGC and OIL have already obtained some data, for making it available, the Government will appropriately compensate them for the cost of acquistion of this data.

(a) whether Government propose to train chilly exporters of Andhra Pradesh on how to preserve chilly for expert and prevent over usage of pesticides and fungicides;

(b) if so, the details thereof; and

(c) whether Government would assist them in exporting the huge stock of chillies lying for exports by opening a regional office of Spices Board in Andhra Pradesh?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE OF THE MINISTRY OF COMMERCE(DR.BOLLA BULLI RAMAIAH)

(a) and (b) Yes Sir. Spices Board jointly with the Horticulture Deptt. of Govt. of Andhra Pradesh and Regional Agriculture Research Institute(RARS), `LAM, Guntur` proposes to conduct training programmes in the district of Guntur, Khammam, Prakasam, Warrangal and Karimnagar for creation of awareness amongst the chilly growers on quality management and post-harvest handling of chillies with emphasis on need based application of pesticides.

(c) Yes Sir. The Spices Board proposes to open an office in Guntur for assisting the growers specially in the areas of quality management and post-harvest handling of storage of chillies for exports.

records.qtitle: GROWTH RATE OF POWER GENERATION .
records.name: Renuka Chowdhury
records.qn_text:
(a) the growth rate of power generation during the financial year 1995-96 and during the period from April to December,1996;

(b) the reasons for the sharp decline;

(c) the targeted rate of growth and estimated achievement during 1996-97;

(d) The steps proposed to be taken to accelerate power generation?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTY FO POWER (DR.S. VENUGOPALACHARI)

(a) and (b) the growth in power generation during 1995-96 and April-December, 1996 over the corresponding period of previous years was 8.3% and 3.5% respectively. The main reason for decline in growth rate of power generation during the current during the current year is fall in hydel power generation.

(c) during April-December, 1996 power generation in the country was 291.5 BU compared to power generation of 281.5 BU during April-December,1995 which represent a growth rate of 3.6% against the target rate of growth of 5.1% fixed for 1996-97

(d) amongst the measures undertaken for increasing power generation are higher utilisation of installed capacity, reducing auxiliary power consumption, modernisation and uprating of existing power stations and initiating schemes for reducing transmission and distribution losses.

records.qtitle: DELAYED IMPLEMENTATION OF PROVERTY ALLEVIATION PROGRAMME IN ANDHRA PRADESH .
records.name: Renuka Chowdhury
records.qn_text:
(a) whether difference between the Andhra Pradesh Government and the Overseas Development Agency (ODA) have delayed implementation of poverty alleviation programmes in 31 municipal towns in the State;

(b) if so, the details thereof; and

(c) the number of slums to be covered under the project, the amount to be spent and the components of which the amount would be spent?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF URBAN AFFAIRS AND EMPLOYMENT AND MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF PARLIAMENTARY AFFAIRS (DR. U. VENKATESWARLU)

(a) to (c) the government of Andhra Pradesh has forward a project proposal covering 23 district headquarters, towns and fast growing urban centers extending the benefit to 1016 slums for assisting the 2,80,786 slum families and covering about 14,55,000 slum population at an estimated cost of Rs. 225 crores for assistance from the overseas.
According to information available with Department of Programme Implementation, as on 31.12. 1996 there were 8 projects under implementation, costing Rs. 50 crores and above in the state of Karnataka/passing through the state of karanataka and were scheduled to be completed during the Eight Five Year Plan. Out of these 8 projects, 3 projects are expected to be completed by the end of Eighth Five Year Plan(31.3.1997) and remaining 5 projects would spill over into the Ninth Plan.

(b) the cost overrun and the anticipated date of completion of 8 projects are given in Statement-I

(c) the projects face various types of problems resulting in time and cost overruns. The list of main factors resulting in time and cost overrun is given in enclosed Statement-II
Development Administration (UK). The project proposal was subsequently revised y the state Government to cover 32 Class-I towns of the State. ODA has suggested for taking up a pilot project in half-a-dozen towns, whereas Government of India wants ODA to cover 32 class-I towns simultaneously.

records.qtitle: PRODUCTION CONSUMPTION AND IMPORT OF CRUDE OIL .
records.name: Renuka Chowdhury
records.qn_text:
(a) the production of crude oil in the nine months of April-December,1996

(b) the estimated consumption of oil during 1995-96 and 1996-97;

(c) the cost of import of oil during this period;

(d) the oil production target for 1996-97 and the actual production likely to be achieved; and

(e) the steps proposed to be taken to accelerate oil production in the country?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF PETROLEUM AND NATURAL GAS (SHRI T.R.BAALU):

(a) to (c) the production , consumption and imports of crude oil during 1995-96 and from April to December, 1996 was as under:-
Production , Consumption and Imports of crude oil (Qty. Million Tonnes) 1995-96 1996-97 April-December

1. Production of Oil 35.145 24.71

2. Consumption of Oil 58.741 46.851

3. Value of imports of crude oil (Rs. crores) Provisional 11517 13940

(d) As against the target of 36.312 MMT the crude oil production during 1996-97 is estimated to be around 33 MMT

(e) Steps taken to accelerate the production of oil in the country are:-
- Implementation of new projects schemes and additional development of existing fields.
- Implementation of EOR schemes and extending some of EOR`s Schemes from pilot scale to full scale field application.

- Implementation of specialized technologies such as ERD, side track, horizontal and drain hole drilling
- Obtaining services of international experts wherever considered necessary.
- 3-D seismic survey of the oil fields
- Rectificatory measures such as aggressive workovers, use of specialized technologies like long/short drift side track, drain hole have been planned for revival of sick wells which still have potential
- Encouraging the participation of private/joint venture in the oil sector
- Enhancing exploration of hydrocarbons and increasing reserves through seismic surveys, deep water explorations, acquisition of acreages/reserves abroad and exploration in frontier areas.

records.qtitle: AMOUNT RECOVERABLE BY IOC FROM INDUSTRY POOL ACCOUNT .
records.name: Renuka Chowdhury
records.qn_text:
(a) whether it is a fact that the Indian Oil Corp. Limited has shown an amount of Rs. 3471 crores against annexure `K` under the heading Investment and 1995-96, as the amount recoverable from the Industry Pool Account, whereas they charged in their Profit and Loss account, net claim of Rs. 2509 crores, from the Industry Pool Account including Rs. 844 crores for the previous year;

(b) if so, what is the justification for showing an inflated amount as their net asset, whereas the net amount charged as Profit and Loss account for 1995-96 is half of figure i.e. Rs. 1165 crores;

(c) whether the recoverable pool account was investigated and audited by C.A.G.; and

(d) if not, what are the reasons for accepting the figures tendered by the Indian Oil Corporation Ltd.?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE IN MINISTRY OF PETORLEUM AND NATURAL GAS (SHRI T.R. BAALU)

(a) Yes, Sir;

(b) It has been reported by the Indian Oil Corporation Limited that the amount shown as recoverable from the account in Schedule K of the Balance Sheet Rs. 3471.28 crores and amount shown in the Income side of Profit and Loss account under the head `Net accounts` Rs. 2509.37 crores are not comparable on account of the following reasons:
(1) The amount shown in the Balance sheet includes unsettled amount carried forward from the previous year whereas the Profit and Loss account reflects the claims lodged- surrenders made during year which may include claims for earlier years also e.g. incentive claim margin updation claims etc. (2) There are certain transactions related to the Balance Sheet, items where claims lodged on OCC such as canalising agent which does not figure in the Profit And Loss Statement reflected in the Balance Sheet
(3) Certain claims from Oil Industries Pool Account such as demurrage on crude oil imports, L/C charges etc. are claimed on Industry basis by IOC and the same are not reflected in the Income side of the P AND L A/c as the same re paid and recovered and accounted under the natural heads of accounts. (4) The amount shown in the Balance-Sheet reflects amount yet to be settled by OCC. It is possible that OCC balance may be negligible at the year end, if OCC is able to settle all the dues during the year.
In view of the above, the amount shown under Profit and Loss account and Balance Sheet cannot be related and depending upon the actual cash settlement taken place and the fund position with OCC, the outstanding balance shown in the Balance Sheet could be totally different from the amount indicated in the P and l Account.

(c) and (d) CAG has audited and viewed the accounts of the company in terms of Section 619(4) of Companies Act, 1956.

records.qtitle: OFFICIAL SECRETS ACT .
records.name: Renuka Chowdhury
records.qn_text:
(a) whether access to information is governed by the Official Secrets Act, 1923; and

(b) if so, by when government proposes to amend the Act and enact laws which give citizens a general right to get access to Government documents with stipulated exceptions?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HOME AFFAIRS (SHRI MOHD, MAQBOOL DAR)

(a) Access to Official information is subject top the provisions of the Official Secrets Act, 1993

(b) a working group has been set up by the Government to examine the possibility of introducing a legislation on Right to Information at the levels of Central and State Government as well as consideration of amendment to various relevant legislation`s including the Official Secrets Act. Further action in this regard in contingent upon the receipt of the above mentioned working Groups` Report which is expected shortly.

records.qtitle: ESTIMATES OF BLACK MONEY
records.name: Renuka Chowdhury
records.qn_text:
(a) the amount of black money estimated to be in existence in the country;

(b) the reasons behind the generation of such huge quantity of black money;

(c) the effect it is showing on the economy of the country; and

(d) steps proposed to be taken to curtail the evil?
records.ans_text:
THE MINISTER OF FINANCE (SHRI P.CHIDAMBARAM)

(a) As per the study made by National Institute of Public Finance and Policy (NIPFP) in 1983-84, black money (in the sense of tax evaded income) was estimated between Rs. 31584 crores to Rs. 36786 crores.

(b) The reasons behind generation of huge quantity of black money, as identified by NIPFP, were the high level of taxation, slackness in tax administration, excessive controls on economic activities, general laws and regulations high inflation rates etc.

(c) In the NIPFP`s study some of the economic consequences of black money have been mentioned as mis-information about the actual state of the economy, loss of revenue, adverse implication for resource allocation, income distribution, and monetary policy etc.

(d) The Government have been taking necessary legislative, fiscal and administrative measures, as deemed appropriate, from time to time to curb the growth of black money.

records.qtitle: PROPOSAL TO INCREASE MINIMUM STATUTORY PRICE OF SUGARCANE .
records.name: Renuka Chowdhury
records.qn_text:
(a) whether the Monopolies and Restrictive Trade Practices Commission (MRTPC) has alleged that Food Corporation of India has been over charging customers and supplying inferior grainst;

(b) if so, the details thereof; and

(c) action taken to set aside money for public welfare as suggested by MRTPC?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF FOOD AND MINISTER OF CIVIL SUPPLIES, DISTRIBUTION (SHRI DEVENDRA PRASAD YADAV)

(a) Yes, Madam, monopolies and Restrictive Trade Practices Commission (MRTPC) has issued notice to the Food Corporation of India on the basis of C&AG Report that it has overcharged the consumers by issuing lower groups of rice in higher group especially in the State of Kerala.

(b) The MRTPC has highlighted that the lower group stocks were issued in the higher group for which the rates of latter groups were charged. It was alleged that the Food Corporation of India has earned an amount of Rs. 418.71 lakhs and customers were overcharged to that extent.

(c) The Food Corporation of India has given a detailed reply to the MRTPC listing therein the procedure being followed in the issue of rice under Public Distribution System (PDS).
There is no excess amount received by the Corporation on account of issue of rice from lower group as higher group or voice versa since the same is adjusted in the amount of subsidy being given by the Government to the Corporation. The FCI has decided to issue the stocks of rice to the PDS only after the receipt of despatch documents by the consigness instead of issuing on the basis of spot findings of the Committee of Officers nominated for the purpose. This would create a little inconvenience to the consumers in places where smaller capacity godowns are located.

records.qtitle: EXEMPTION FROM COMPULSORY USE OF JUTE BAG PACKING .
records.name: Renuka Chowdhury
records.qn_text:
(a) whether the Andhra Pradesh Cement Producers` Association have sought exemption from compulsory use of Jute bag packing for cement industry;

(b) the reasons for seeking exemptions;

(c) the reaction of Government thereto; and

(d) whether Government propose to amend the Jute Packaing Material (Compulsory Use in the Packaging Material (Compulsory Use in the Packaging Commodities) Act, 1995; if so, the details thereof?
records.ans_text:
THE MINISTER OF TEXTILES (SHRI R.L.JALAPPA):

(a) Yes, Sir.

(b) and (c) The reasons advanced by the Andhra Pradesh Cement Producers Associations, inter-alia are that the packing in Jute bage is resulting in seepage loss, degradation, adulteration, dust pollution, etc. It is also mentioned that the price of Cement Gunny Bags is costlier than the HDPE/Paper Bags. Their request has been placed before the standing Advisory Committee set up by the Government in terms of Section 4 (I) of the Jute Packaging Material

(Compulsory Use in Packing Commodities Act, 1907).

(d) No, Sir.

records.qtitle: FEASIBILITY OF SETTING UP A PASSENGER CAR PLANT IN VISAKHAPATNAM OR KAKINADA. .
records.name: Renuka Chowdhury
records.qn_text:
(a) whether the Andhra Pradesh Government has requested the Central Government to examine the feasibility of setting up a passenger car plant in the port cities of Visakhapatnam or Kakinada; and

(b) if so, the action taken thereon
records.ans_text:
:- THE MINISTER OF INDUSTRY (SHRI MURASOLI MARAN)

(a) and (b) Yes, Sir. A request has been received from Andhra Pradesh Government for setting up of a passenger car plant by M/s. Maruti Udyog Limited

(MUL) in the port cities of Visakhapatnam or Kakinada. Since MUL is a non- Government Company and a view on the location of the plant is therefore to be taken by MUL Board of Directors; the matter has been referred to MUL.

records.qtitle: ANDHRA PRADESH GOVERNMENT S PROPOSALS FOR ASSISTANCE UNDER NATIONAL RENEWAL FUND .
records.name: Renuka Chowdhury
records.qn_text:
(a) whether the Andhra Pradesh Government has submitted proposals for assistance under the National Renewal Fund in view of excessive work force in certain units;

(b) if so, the amount proposed to be sanctioned towards Voluntary Retirement Scheme in the case of Allwyn Auto Limited and Republic Forge Co. Ltd. as the units are not viable; and

(c) when decisions in this regard are likely to be finalised in view of financial constraints of the State Government?
records.ans_text:
:- THE MINISTER OF INDUSTRY (SHRI MURASOLI MARAN):

(a) to (c) Yes, Sir. But assistance from NRF is presently restricted only to Voluntary Retirement Scheme in Central Public Sector Undertakings and to the schemes for counselling, retraining and redeployment assistance to rationalised workers.

records.qtitle: LOSSES INCURRED BY MMTC .
records.name: Renuka Chowdhury
records.qn_text:
(a) whether attention of the Government has been drawn to the news item appearing in the Indian Express dated 29th September, 1966, captioned `MMTC incurs losses due to irregularities`

(b) if so, the facts thereof; and

(c) the remedial steps taken to set right the working of the Mineral and Metals Trading Corporation?
records.ans_text:
:- THE MINISTER OF STATE OF THE MINISTRY OF COMMERCE (SHRI BOLLA BULLI RAMAIAH)

(a) There is no News Item in Indian Express dated 29th September` 96 captioned `MMTC incures losses due to irregulatities`.However, Hon`ble MP possibly refers to the News Item in the Indian Express dated 26th September` 96

(b) and (c) The Information is being collected and shall be laid on the Table of the House.

records.qtitle: OECF FUND FOR POWER PROJECTS IN ANDHRA PRADESH .
records.name: Renuka Chowdhury
records.qn_text:
(a) whether Andhra Pradesh Government has requested to get the Simhadri Power project at Visakhapatnam and Krishnapatnam Thermal Power Station in Nellore district processed for inclusion under OECF funding for the current and the coming year;

(b) if so, the details thereof; and

(c) the action taken to get the project cleared in the interest of development of the State?
records.ans_text:
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF POWER AND MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF NON-CONVENTIONAL ENERGY SOURCES (DR. S. VENUGOPALACHARI):

(a) to (c): Andhra pradesh Government/Andhra Pradesh State Electricity Board (APSEB) have requested assistance for several new power projects including Transmission Schemes for evacuation of power from Vizag, Simhadri and Krishnapatnam TPSs under OECF 1997-98 loan package. However, after discussions with APSEB and keeping in view the preparedness of the related generation projects, Ministry of Finance has been requested to pose the Integrated Transmission Scheme to evacuate power from Vizag and Simhadri TPSs at an estimated cost of Rs. 809 crores to the Government of Japan/OECF. Simhadri Thermal Power Generation Project State I (2 x 500 MW) of National Thermal Power Corporation in Andhra Pradesh has already been agreed to be funded by the Government of Japan under the 1996-97 OECF loan package.

records.qtitle: DECF S ASSISTANCE FOR TAIL POND DAM POWER HOUSE PROJECTS IN ANDHRA PRADESH .
records.name: Renuka Chowdhury
records.qn_text:
(a) whether the Andhra Pradesh Government has requested to recommend the projects relating to Tail Pond Dam Power House (down stream of Nagarjuna sagar) to the overseas economic cooperation fund (DECF) for assistance;

(b) if so, the details thereof; and

(c) the steps proposed to be taken for arranging external assistance for early implementation of the project?
records.ans_text:
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF POWER AND MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF NON-CONVENTIONAL ENERGY SOURCES (DR. S. VENUGOPALACHARI):

(a) to (c) Andhra Pradesh State Electricity Board (APSEB) had requested Government of India to pose Nagarjuna Sagar Tail Pond Dam Power House hydroelectric scheme (2x25 MW) for external funding during the 9th Plan period. The project can be posed for external assistance only after the project receives clearance from Ministry of Environment & Forests and investment approval from Planning Commission.

records.qtitle: FUNDS TO HELP INJURED ARMY PERSONEL .
records.name: Renuka Chowdhury
records.qn_text:
(a) whether it is a fact that there is shortage of funds to help injured armymen

(b) if so, the details thereof; and

(c) the action taken to look after the injured armymen with full care especially in Paraplegic Rehabilitation Centre, Kirkee?
records.ans_text:
THE MINISTER OF DEFENCE (SHRI MULAYAM SINGH YADAV):

(a) to (c) The injured Army men are treated in various Military Hospitals and in the Paraplegic Rehabilitation Centre, Kirkee. The Military Hospitals are given adequate funds from the budget grant. The Paraplegic Rehabilitation Centre, Kirkee was established in 1978 with a financial assistance of Rs. 12,28,700/- from National Defence Fund. The Paraplegic Centre is autonomous in its functioning and all dicisions regarding pay and allowances of the staff, management of establishment and expenditure on paraplegics, are taken by its Boar of Trustees/Management Committee. The Paraplegic Rehabilitation Centre has its own corpus of funds, the interest earnings of which are utlised for its running. In addition, the Kendriya Sainik Board also privides annual grant for the maintenance of the establishment and the up-keep of the inmates. During the last 5 years the Paraplegic Rehabilitation Centre has been given following financial assistance by the Kendriya sainik Board:- 
Year                          Amount
1992-93                       Rs.  14,87,836/-
1993-94                       Rs.  7,23,046/-
1994-95                       Rs.  12,73,900/-
1995-96                       Rs.  12,60,162/-
1996-97                       Rs.  15,96,565/-
At present, the Paraplegic Rehabilitation Centre, Pune has 75 inmates, with a
staff of 53 employees including 19 Attendants, 1 Medical Superintendent, 2
Physiotherapists and 2 Nursing Assistants.

records.qtitle: INTERNAL IDBT .
records.name: Renuka Chowdhury
records.qn_text:
(a) the details of burgeoing internal debt and other liabilities of the Central Government; and

(b) the corrective financial measures proposed to ourtail the growth of Government debt?
records.ans_text:
THE MINISTER OF FINANCE (SHRI P. CHIDAMBARAM):

(a) The Internal debt and other liabilities at the end of 1995-96 (RE) were as under:- (Rs. crore)

(i) Internal debt (Market loans, Treasury Bills, 303358.86 Relief Bonds etc.)

(ii) Other liabilities (Small Savings Schemes, 249685.31 Provident Funds, Reserve Funds and Deposits etc.)

(b) The Government would endeavour to contain the fiscal deficit (additional borrowings) in the current year at 5% of GDP by increasing receipts and contraling expenditure.

records.qtitle: PROTECTION OF FISHERMEN IN ORISSA
records.name: Renuka Chowdhury
records.qn_text:
(a) whether scores of lives of fishermen and fishing boats were lost in recent cyclonic storm into the Orissa waters;

(b) whether Government propose to set-up three relay stations of AIR at Sompeta. Kakinada and Nellore to cover the shadow regions beyond orissa and Andhra Pradesh border to apprise fishermen of weather bulletins in time; and

(c) the other steps proposed to protect the local fishermen from impending dangers of cyclone in coastal areas?
records.ans_text:
THE MINISTER OF AGRICULTURE(SHRI CHATURANAN MISHRA)

(a) No, Sir.

(b) The coastal areas of Orissa and Andhra Pradesh including Sompeta, Kakinadaand Nellore fall within the coverage zone of the High Power Transmitters atCuttack, Vijayawada and Vishakhapatnam and FM Transmitters at Puri and Behrampur.

(c) Cyclone warning dissemination system has been set up in the coastal areas for relaying regular weather bulletins for the benefit of the vulnerable people including fishermen.

records.qtitle: SETTING UP OF DRAVIDIAN UNIVERSITY
records.name: Renuka Chowdhury
records.qn_text:
(a) whether a Dravidian University is being set-up to develop Dravidian and tribal lanugages;

(b) if so, the details including the significance thereof; and

(c) the contribution proposed to be given by Government in this regard?
records.ans_text:
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE DEPARTMENT OF EDUCATION IN THE MINISTRY OF HUMAN RESOURCE DEVELOPMENT(SHRI MUHI RAM SAIKIA): (a) and (b) The Central Government has no proposal, at present, to set up any University for Dravidian and tribal Languages. The State Government of Andhra Pradesh has, however, proposed to set up one such University at Kuppam in Andhra Pradesh in collaboration with the State Governments of Kerala, Karnataka and Tamil Nadu.

(c) There is no proposal under consideration of the Govt. of India to provide any grant towards the capital cost of any such University.

records.qtitle: FUNDS FOR KOTHAGUNDEM THERMAL POWER STATION .
records.name: Renuka Chowdhury
records.qn_text:
(a) whether Government have received any request from the Andhra Pradesh Government for release of funds for the works on stage V of Kothagundem thermal power station ;

(b) if so, the details thereof ; and

(c) the action taken by Government to release the funds at any early date ?
records.ans_text:
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF POWER AND MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF NON-CONVENTIONAL ENERGY SOURCES (DR. S. VENUGOPALACHARI):

(a) and (b) Andhra Pradesh State Electricity Board (APSEB) have requested Power Finance Corporation (PFC) for a term loan assistance of Rs.500 crores for completion of Stage V (2 250 MW) Units 9 & 10 Kothagundem Thermal Power Station.

(c) PFC have sanctioned a loan of Rs.130 crores in August, 1996 to APSEB towards completion of balance works in respect of Unit 9, programmed to be synchronised by March, 1997 .

records.qtitle: URBAN DECONGESTION PROGRAMME FOR HYDERABAD .
records.name: Renuka Chowdhury
records.qn_text:
(a) whether the Andhra Pradesh Government has requested for arranging international funding for taking up an urban decongestion programme for Hyderabad Metropolitan area and also for water supply and sewer projects in District Head Quarter towns

(b) if so, the details thereof; and

(c) the action taken thereon?
records.ans_text:
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF URBAN AFFAIRS & EMPLOYMENT & MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF PARLIAMENTARY AFFAIRS (DR. U. VENKATESWARLU): (a) Yes, Sir. During January, 1995, the State Government has requested for obtaining international funding to undertake civic amenities in urban areas of Andhra Pradesh.

(b) The detailed project proposals are awaited from the Government of Andhra Pradesh.

(c) The matter was taken up with the Asian Development Bank (ADB) and the Bank has included Andhra Pradesh as one of the `focus` states.  1106

records.qtitle: RESTRUCTURING AND REVIVAL OF HINDUSTAN SHIPYARD VISAKHAPATNAM .
records.name: Renuka Chowdhury
records.qn_text:
(a) whether the Andhra Pradesh Government has given representation for capital restructuring and revival of Hindustan Shipyard Limited, Visakhapatnam;

(b) the assistance sought for and proposed to be released; and

(c) the policy of direct support for survival of Indian ship building yards?
records.ans_text:
:- THE MINISTER OF SURFACE TRANSPORT (SHRI G. VENKATRAMAN):

(a) to (c) The Chief Minister of Andhra Pradesh, while forwarding on 15.7.96 the representation of Telugunadu Trade Union Council (TNTUC) unit, Hindustan Shipyard Ltd., Visakhapatnam had requested for capital restructuring of HSL and continuing the Government assistance for shipbuilding industry. Action has since been initiated by the Government to process the proposals relating to capital restructuring of HSL and reintroduction of subsidy scheme.

records.qtitle: DRINKING WATER PROJECTS IN FLOURISIS AFFECTED DISTRICTS OF ANDHRA PRADESH .
records.name: Renuka Chowdhury
records.qn_text:
(a) whether the Andhra Pradesh Government have forwarded proposels for assistance for taking up drinking water projects in seven districts having problems of fluorides or brackash water;

(b) whether large scale cases of death on account of fluorisis have been reported in Andhra Pradesh,

(c) if so, the details thereof; and

(d) the action taken for early sanction of the projects?
records.ans_text:
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF RURAL AREAS & EMPLOYMENT (SHRI CHANDRADEO PRASAD VARMA):

(a) Yes, Sir.

(b) Government of India has not received any such report from the State Government.

(c) does not arise.

(d) Action has been taken to process and sanction the projects in consultation with the State Government.

records.qtitle: INTEGRATED RURAL SANITATION PROJECT .
records.name: Renuka Chowdhury
records.qn_text:
(a) whether Government have introduced Integrated Rural Sanitation Project;

(b) if so, the details thereof;

(c) if not, the steps proposed to construct household sanitation in villages, with a view to improve sanitation in the rural areas; and

(d) the steps taken to clear and sanction such a project proposal submitted by the Andhra Pradesh Government on the 31st October, 1995?
records.ans_text:
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF RURAL AREAS & EMPLOYMENT (SHRI CHANDRADEO PRASAD VERMA):

(a) and (b) Yes, Sir. The Centrally Sponsored Rural Sanitation Programme (CRSP) and State Sector Minimum Needs Programme are under implementation to provide sanitation facilities in the rural areas.

(c) Does not arise.

(d) The Government of Andhra Pradesh sought Rs. 226 crore for provision of sanitation facilities in 22 district. Considering that the total budget under Central Rural Sanitation. Programme is Rs. 60 crore only, the State Government was requested to revise the project like adoption of low cost models of sanitatry Information, Education and Communication (IEC) component for creation of felt need/ demand, health education and awareness, in order to explore the possibility for external assistance also. This revised project is yet to be sent by the State Government.
