(d) and (e) Some of the steps taken by Tobacco Board to enhance production productivity and
quality of tobacco as an incentive to enhance exports are:-


(i) Supply of seeds/seedlings of high yielding and disease resistant varieties of FCV/Burley
tobacco;


(ii) pest and disease control through fumigation of nurseries;


(iii) Encouraging use of sprinkler irrigation system;


(iv) Improving curing and storing facilities;


(v) Arranging supply of inputs such as coal (for curing), fertilisers, and suckerides, and


(vi) training and exposure of farmers to latest research findings.

records.qtitle: RELEASE OF SUGAR UNDER FREE SALE SUGAR QUOTA BY ANDHRA PRADESH .
records.name: Renuka Chowdhury
records.qn_text:
(a) whether the State Government of Andhra Pradesh has requested for release of 20,000 tonnes of sugar under free sale quota;

(b) if so, the details thereof; and

(c) the action taken in the matter?
records.ans_text:
THE MINISTER OF FOOD AND MINISTER OF CIVIL SUPPLIES, CONSUMER AFFAIRS AND PUBLIC DISTRIBUTION

(SHRI DEVENDRA PRASAD YADAV):

(a) to (c) The Government of Andhra Pradesh in June, 1996 requested for release of an additional freesale quota of 20,000 tonnes of sugar in respect of different units of Nizam sugars Ltd. (State owned company), as a special case.
During the month of June, 1996 apart from the normal quota of 7,40,000 Mts. of freesale sugar, an additional quota of 50,000 M. tonnes was released. In addition, the sugar factories were permitted to sell 30% more sugar over and above their quota. As such, it was decided that there was no need to grant further additional freesale quotas to any particular sugar factory.

records.qtitle: INCREASE IN THE SUBSIDY ON SERICULTURE .
records.name: Renuka Chowdhury
records.qn_text:
(a) whether Government of Andhra Pradesh has represented for increasing the subsidy on sericulture;

(b) if so, the details thereof;

(c) the action taken thereon; and

(d) the measures taken to increase the subsidy to boost export of silk? ANSWER
records.ans_text:
THE MINISTER OF TEXTILES (SHRI R. L. JALAPPA):

(a) Yes, Sir.

(b) and (c) The Central Silk Board has received requests/suggestions from sericulture States

(including Andhra Pradesh) for grant of subsidy for drip irrigation in sericulture sector. After examining/considering the various proposals/requests/suggestions, the Central Silk Board has recently drafted a scheme for providing subsidy for installation of drip irrigation system.

(d) Under the existing Export-Import Policy there are no restrictions on export of silk. However, in order to maximise foreign exchange earnings, the Government encourages export of value added silk products instead of raw silk.

records.qtitle: CANCER FROM MOBILE PHONE .
records.name: Renuka Chowdhury
records.qn_text:
(a) whether cellular phones cause brin demange and cancer;

(b) whether mobile phone operators suffer from constrant headaches and watering of eyes for months and the use of mobile phones has been stopped in advanced countries;

(c) whether Government propose to assess the health and environmental effects of exposure to electric and magnetic filds of mobile phones; and

(d) if so, the details thereof and if not, the reasons therefor?
records.ans_text:
THE MINISTER OF COMMUNICATIONS (SHRI BENI PRASAD VERMA):

(a) and (b) No confirmed incidence has been reported in this regard.

(c) There is no such proposal.

(d) Does not arise in view of (a) and (b) above.

records.qtitle: PROJECTS TO BE TAKEN UP UNDER NHPP IN ANDHRA PRADESH .
records.name: Renuka Chowdhury
records.qn_text:
(a) the details of the projects to be taken up in Andhra Pradesh under the National Hydrology Project Programme Proposed to be taken up with world Bank; and

(b) the target for completion of the projects? ANSWER

records.qtitle: POLICY REGARDING PROFITS EARNED THROUGH EXPORTS .
records.name: Renuka Chowdhury
records.qn_text:
(a) whether it is a fact that profits earned through export business were exempted from taxes;

(b) whether the new policy announced recently regarding profits earned through export is going to hinder export trade; and

(c) what is the expected revenue gain if the new policy is implemented?
records.ans_text:
THE MINISTER OF FINANCE (SHRI P. CHIDAMBARAM):

(a) Yes, Madam.

(b) Some export companies may have to pay tax under the proposed Minimum Alternate Tax provisions.

(c) The expected revenue gain on account of Minimum Alternate Tax provisions is Rs. 2,000.00 crores approximately in a full year.

records.qtitle: PLANS TO REDUCE INCREASING INTEREST BURDEN .
records.name: Renuka Chowdhury
records.qn_text:
(a) whether Government are planning to reduce the increasing interest burden which is around Rs. 60,000 crores; and

(b) if so, how and when, details thereof?
records.ans_text:
THE MINISTER OF FINANCE (SHRI P. CHIDAMBARAM):

(a) and (b) Growth in interest expenditure can be contained only through reducation in fiscal deficit which represents the total borrowings by the Government in a year for financing its expenditure. The rise in interest payments is a sequel to the borrowings undertaken each year for financing plan expenditure. Government would, however, endeavour to contain fiscal deficit by maximising the revenues and controlling the expenditure which will help in reducing the interest burden. On the recommendation of the Standing Committee on Finance, the Central Government requested Reserve Bank of India to carry out a study on the rising interest payments. The report submitted by the Reserve Bank of India is being examined by an Inter Ministerial Group.

records.qtitle: QUALITY CUT OF PADDY TO THE STATE GOVERNMENT BY FCI .
records.name: Renuka Chowdhury
records.qn_text:
(a) whether Government of Andhra Pradesh have represented for payment of Rs. 16.80 crores towards quality of paddy (ric

(e) to the State Government by the FCI;

(b) if so, the reaction of Government thereto;

(c) whether necessary instructions to the FCI for carly payment has been issued; and

(d) when the payment is likely to be made?
records.ans_text:
THE MINISTER OF FOOD AND MINISTER OF CIVIL SUPPLIES, CONSUMER AFFAIRS AND PUBLIC DISTRIBUTION (SHRI DEVENDRA PRASAD YADV):

(a) Yes, Sir.

(b) to (d) Upto 1994-95 rice used to be procured if the quality was within the prescribed range i.e. between tolerance limit and rejection limit. With the adoption of single grade specifications` in respect of rice the scope of value cuts has been reduced considerably. However, in 1995-96 rice marketing season, on requests of certain State Govts., quality parameters were relaxed subject to value cuts in respect of only 4 out of 9 parameters. Whatever quality cuts are made,they get reflected in the reduced pooled cost of foodgrain with the FCI. Economic cost of rice, even with the value cuts, remains much higher than the Central Issue Price is fixed by the Govt. conforming to the standards under Prevention of Food Adulteration Act and these specifications remain the same for the whole country. In view of this, the amount of quality cuts cannot be passed on to the concerned Statc/UTs.

records.qtitle: DIFFERENCE IN PROCUREMENT PRICE OF PADDY IN PUNJAB AND ANDHRA PRADESH
records.name: Renuka Chowdhury

records.qtitle: INCREASING SUBSIDY ON DRIP IRRIGATION FOR OILPALM .
records.name: Renuka Chowdhury
records.qn_text:
(a) whether Government of Andhra Pradesh has represented for increasing the subsidy for providing drip irrigation for oilpalm;

(b) if so, the details thereof;

(c) the action taken thereon; and

(d) the measures taken to increase the subsidy to boost export of oilpalm?
records.ans_text:
HE MINISTER OF AGRICULTURE (SHRI CHATURANAN MISHRA):

(a) and (b) The Government of Andhra Pradesh had represented for increasing subsidy at par with horticultural creps, which meant increasing subsidy for installation of drip irrigation system for oil palm growers from Rs. 10,000 per hectare to Rs. 15,000 per hectare, or 50% of cost of installation, whichever is less. The Government of Andhra Pradesh also sought relaxation in restriction of area from 1 hectare to 6 hectares and increase in funding pattern from 80:20 to 90:10 sharing basis between Government of India and State Government.

(c) The Government of India raised the subsidy to Oil Palm growers from Rs. 10,000 to Rs. 15,000 per hectare and relaxed the restriction of area to 6 hectares for installation of drip irrigation system for the year 1995-96. Further, the subsidy borne by Government of India with State Governments was revised from 80:20 to 90:10 sharing basis. For the year 1996-97, the matter is under consideration of the Government.

(d) No measures have so far been taken to increase export of Oil Palm.

records.qtitle: MODEL FLORICULTURE CENTRE AT HYDERABAD .
records.name: Renuka Chowdhury
records.qn_text:
(a) whether Government of Andhra Pradesh have requested for sanction of a Model Floriculture Centre at Hyderabad in view of a large number of foreign collaborations in floriculture in Andhra Pradesh;

(b) if so, the details thereof; and

(c) the action taken thereon?
records.ans_text:
THE MINISTER OF AGRICULTURE (SHRI CHATURANAN MISHRA):

(a) Yes, Sir.

(b) and (c) The Government of India has sanctioned setting up of a Model Floriculture Centre in the State of Andhra Pradesh at a total cost of Rs. 57.50 lakhs, under the Central Sector Scheme on Commercial Floriculture. The Centre would serve as the focal unit for floriculture development in the State and will undertake collection, multiplication and distribution of quality planting material of improved varieties; laying out demonstrations on new technologies and training of farmers/entrepreneur on various aspects related to production and post harvest management of flower crops.

records.qtitle: RELEASE OF RELIEF FUND .
records.name: Renuka Chowdhury
records.qn_text:
(a) whether the fund sanctioned by the National Relief Committee for heavy rains and floods in October, 1995, have not yet been released;

(b) if so, the reasons therefor; and

(c) the steps taken for ealry release of the fund?
records.ans_text:
THE MINISTER OF AGRICULTURE (SHRI CHATURANAN MISHRA):

(a) Funds aggregataing Rs. 104.00 crores approved by the National Calamity Relief Committee as assistance from the National Fund for Calamity Relief to the six States of Andhra Pradesh, Arunachal Pradesh, Bihar, Meghalaya, Rajasthan and West Bengal in the wake of floods of September-October, 1995 have been released on 23rd August, 1996.

(b) and (c) Do not arise.

records.qtitle: INTRODUCTION OF LOK PAL BILL
records.name: Renuka Chowdhury
records.qn_text:
(a) Whether it is a fact that Government propose to introduce the Lok Pal Bill in the current Session of the Parliament;

(b) if so, what are the salient feature of the proposed Bill; and

(c) what are the other details in this regard?
records.ans_text: THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF PERSONNEL PUBLIC GRIEVANCES AND PENSIONS (SHRIMATI MARGARET ALVA): (a) to (c) Yes, Sir. The government proposal to introduce the Lockpal Bill during the current Session of Parliament.

records.qtitle: RAILWAY NETWORK BETWEEN RENIGUNTA AND GUDUR
records.name: Renuka Chowdhury
records.qn_text:
(a) Whether Government propose to set-up railway network between Renigunta and Gudur;

(b) If so, the details thereof;

(c) By when will the electrification work between Renigunta and Hospet be taken-up;

(d) The approximate expenditure on the project; and

(e) The target for the completion of the project?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF RAILWAYS (SHRI SATPAL MAHARAJ)

(a) and (b) Gudur and Renigunta stations are already connected by a broad gauge railway line and are on the national rail network.

(c)to (e) The electrification of Rentigunta-Hospet section is an approved work but due to resource crunch, the work has been pended for the time being.

records.qtitle: NATIONAL POLICY FOR EMPOWERMENT OF .
records.name: Renuka Chowdhury
records.qn_text:
(a) Whether a draft national policy for the empowerment of womeninto defacto power sharing equality is being chalked out;

(b) If so, the details thereof; and

(c) By when will it be finalised?
records.ans_text:
MINISTER OF HUMAN RESOURCE DEVELOPMENT (SHRI S.R. BOMMAI):

(a) to (c) A draft national policy for the empowerment of women has already been finalised. A copy is given in the annexure.

(See Appendix 180, annexure NO.2)

records.qtitle: CASE AGAINST ITDC OFFICIALS BY CBI .
records.name: Renuka Chowdhury
records.qn_text:
(a) whether CBI is contemplating to register a case of duping ITDC of Rs. 12.00 lacs;

(b) whether it is a fact that in the said case CBI indicated some officers of ITDC;

(c) whether it is also a fact that no action has been taken in the said case as recommended by CBI; and

(d) if so, what action Government propose to take against the Disciplinary Authority for not taking action?
records.ans_text:
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF CIVIL AVAITION AND TOURISM: (SHRI GHULAM NABI AZAD):

(a) to (d) CBI had registered a regular case on 11.3. 93 against Shri Ramdass under Section 420 IPC for deceiving the Ashok Hotel to the tune of Rs. 1147545.87 CBI has reported in March 1993 that Shri Ramdass was arrested and remanded to judicial custody. CBI subsequently filed as charge sheet on 9.11.93 in the court of Metropolitan Magistrate, Delhi against Shri Ramdass and M/s durga containers Ltd. The case is pending trail at final stage. No officer of ITDC has been indicted in the said case.

records.qtitle: INAUGURAL FUNCTION OF BAGIYA RESTAURANT WITHOUT COMPLETING AGREEMENT .
records.name: Renuka Chowdhury
records.qn_text:
(a) whether it is a fact that the then C & MD, ITDC prescribed over the inaugural function of Bagiya Restaurant on 2nd November, 1994;

(b) whether it is a fact that formal written agreement between ITDC and Excel Hotels and Restaurant Incharge was signed on 10th November, 1994;

(c) whether it is a fact that no records was maintained by ITDC/ Ashok Yatri Niwas regarding exact date of handling over the premises of Bagiya Restaurant to Excel Hotels and Restaurant Incharge; and

(d) if answer to

(a),

(b) and

(c) is yes, why the then C & MD, ITDC was allowed to inaugurate Bagiya Restaurant without completing essential formalities like signing of agreement and handling over the physical possession of the premises etc? ANSWER
records.ans_text:
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF CIVIL AVIATION AND TOURISM (SHRI GHULAM NABI AZAD) :

(a) to (c) Yes, Sir.

(b) The matter is under examination.

records.qtitle: ENQUIRY INTO THE BAGIYA RESTAURANT EPISODE .
records.name: Renuka Chowdhury
records.ans_text:
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF CIVIL AVIATION AND TOURISM (SHRI GHULAM NABI AZAD ) :

(a) and (b) The Director General of Tourism was asked to conduct an enquiry into the alleged irregularities in the award of licence of Bagiya Restaurant in Ashok Yatri Niwas of ITDC. His report was received by the Government on 31.7.95 and on the basis of findings contained therein, the matter has been referred to CBI for a detailed enquiry. CBI has already registered the case on 4.9.95 against the followings :

1. Shri. M.N. Gupta, Vice Present, ITDC

2. Shri K.K. Tuli, General Manager, Ashok Yatri Niwas, ITDC, New Delhi

3. Shri C.S. Jain, G.M. ITDC

4. Shri L.M. Batra, Resident Manager, ITDC

5. Caption R.R. Arora, Manager, ITDC 6. Shri Vijay Kumar, chief Acct. Officer ITDC

7 M/s. Exel Hotels, & Restaurants, ICN, 159, Kamla Market, N. Delhi. The report of the CBI in the matter in awaited. In addition an internal inquiry was ordered by ITDC. The report of that inquiry has been received and is under examination.

records.qtitle: AUDITING THE EXPENSES OF POLITICAL PARTIES .
records.name: Renuka Chowdhury
records.qn_text:
(a) whether it is a fact that Election Commission has recommended to the Law Ministry to bring an enactment for auditing the expenses of the political parties;

(b) if so, what are the provisions proposed by the Election Commission for enactment of such a law;

(c) why such a law has not been formulated so far; and

(d) whether it is a fact that restrictions on expenses of individual candidates is negated by the huge expense of the political parties?
records.ans_text:
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF LAW, JUSTICE AND COMPANY AFFAIRS: (SHRI H.R. BHARDWAJ):

(a) and (b) The Election Commission has, from time to time, among other proposals, also made a proposal for compulsory maintenance of accounts of political parties and audit thereof by agencies specified by the Election Commission.

(c) There has been no unanimity of views amongst political parties on the said proposal. The Dinesh Goswami Committee which had examined the proposal had also decided not to pursue it.

(d) Government has no information in this regard.

records.qtitle: ALLOCATION OF MATCH WAX .
records.name: Renuka Chowdhury
records.qn_text:
(a) what are the criteria followed by the Ministry regarding allocation `of Match-Wax to different States;

(b) whether any Match-Wax has been released to the State of Haryana in the last three years; if so, what quantities and on what basis; and

(c) by when the present demand of the State of Haryana for a regular supply of Match-Wax is likely to be met and what -shall be the quantities for the forthcoming quarters of this year and next year?
records.ans_text:
THE MINISTER OF STATE OF THE MINISTRY OF PETROLEUM AND NATURAL GAS (CAPTAIN SATISH SHARMA):

(a) to (c) Paraffin Wax-type-3 (Match Wax) is allocated to various States based on the assessed capacities of units registered before 30.6.1986 on prorata basis subject to availability. Haryana State was allocated 300 MTs of Match wax in the year 1993 and 30 Mts. in the IInd quarter of 1995 on adhoc basis. Satisfaction of demand of States/UTs is dependent on the overall product availability in a particular year. To make easy availability of the product, import of paraffin wax has been decanalised w.e.f. 1.4.92 and any user or State Government can import the same to meet its demands.

records.qtitle: COST PER MW OF POWER PROJECTS .
records.name: Renuka Chowdhury
records.qn_text:
(a) whether it is a fact that Thermal Power Project or a combined Cycle Gas Project do not cost more than Rupees 2 crore per MW, taking into account equipment cost alone;

(b) whether it is a fact that price at which power is supplied to the grid should not exceed 4.2 cents a unit; and

(c) whether Government have voted that multinationals are forming carted to fleece India?
records.ans_text:
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF POWER (SHRIMATI URMILABEN CHIMANBHAI PATIL):

(a) The cost per MW of equipment alone is less than Rs. 2.00 crores in respect of the projects recently commissioned/under implementation and exceeds Rs. 2.00 crores in respect of new projects.

(b) Tarrif is a derivative of capital cost as approved by the Central Electricity Authority. Once the capital cost has been approved, it is calculated on the basis of principles (norms & parameters) notified by the Government in this regard from time to time.

(c) No, Sir.

records.qtitle: INVESTIGATIONS OF HAWALA CASES .
records.name: Renuka Chowdhury
records.qn_text:
(a) whether it is a fact that Senior Officers who were investigating Hawala Case involving Jain brothers and politicians have been shifted from their current jobs; and

(b) whether their transfer was stayed by the Supreme Court?
records.ans_text:
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF FINANCE (SHRI M. V. CHANDRASHEKHAR MURTHY):

(a) and (b) The then Director of Enforcement, Sir Javed Chowdhury, was relieved on promotion as Additional Secretary. Sir Amod Kanth, who had been functioning as Deputy Inspector General in the Central Bureau of Investigation, was relieved on completion of his tenure. No stay orders were issued by the Supreme Court in these cases.

records.qtitle: COMPUTER SOFTWARE SECTORS IN EUROPEAN UNION AND JAPAN .
records.name: Renuka Chowdhury
records.qn_text:
(a) whether it is a fact that neither the European Union nor Japan have agreed to open up their Computer Software sectors to foreign officials;

(b) whether U.S. has liberalised entry of Computer Software; and

(c) if so, the details thereof?
records.ans_text:
THE MINISTER OF STATE OF THE MINISTRY OF COMMERCE (SHRI P. CHIDAMBARAM):

(a) to (c) As a part of the Uruguay Round Market Access package on Services, the US, the European Union (EU) and Japan have undertaken to liberalise market access in the computer and related services sector. As far as access to foreign service providers in this sector is concerned, all three have undertaken to bind commitments on the entry of natural persons with commercial presence viz; intra-corporate transferes and business visitors.
In addition, the US and European Union have also undertaken to liberlise the entry of natural persons as service providers without commercial presence.

records.qtitle: CRIMINAL POLITICIAN NEXUS .
records.name: Renuka Chowdhury
records.qn_text:
(a) whether Government`s attention has been drawn to the newsitem published in the `Time of India` on 14th July, 1995 entitled as `Criminal politician nexus causes concern` and

(b) if so, what are the counter measures on legal, political and administrative plans?
records.ans_text:
THE MINISTER OF STATE OF THE MINISTRY OF HOME AFFAIRS (SHRI RAJESH PILOT):

(a) Yes, Sir.

(b) Report of Vohra Committee established to take stock of all available information about the activities of crime Syndicates Mafia organisation which had developed links with and were being protected by Govt. functionaries and political personalities has been laid on the Table of both the Houes on 01-08- 1995. Based on the recommendations of the Committee a Nodal Group under the Chairmanship of Home Secretary has been constituted to collect and collate the information and to decide on the action that is required to be taken to ensure that the nexus of criminals with businessmen, politicians or bureaucrats is broken.

records.qtitle: ENACTMENT OF LOK PAL BILL .SHRI CHIMANBHAI MEHTA
records.name: Renuka Chowdhury
records.qn_text: (a) the response of othe leaders of all the political parties to the letter addressed by
records.ans_text:
the Minister of State for Personnel Public Grievances and Pensions on 31st May, 1995 asking for comments to bring about consensus the enactment of Lokpal Bill in the current Session; and

(b) the names of leaders or MPs who have responded to the invitation to send suggestion on Lokpal including the response of major National parties and by when Government are planning to call a meeting of all political parties and groups to find out a consensus? ANSWER THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF PERSONNEL, PUBLIC GRIEVANCES AND PENSIONS (SMT. MARGARET ALVA):

(a) 49 Hon`ble Member of Parliament were addressed out of which 5 Member have responded till 28.07.95.

(b) Shri E. Ahamed, Muslim League, Shri Jaswant Singh, BJP, Shri Chimanbhai Mehta, Independent, Ms. Dil Kumari Bhandari, SSP, Shri Chaturanan Mishra, have responded to the inviation of M of MOS (PP). Shri Jaswant Singh has suggested that the matter be left the next Lok Sabha. MR. CHAIRMAN: Please put the question. SHRI CHIMANBHAI MEHTA: Therefore, my question is, when are you going to call a meeting to bring about a consensus on the Lokpal Bill? That is my main point. SMT. MARGARET ALVA: Sir, I am sorry, but I would like to draw the attention of the hon. Member to this . He says that my answer is irrelevant. The first part of the question is about the response of the leaders of all the political parties to the letter addressed by the Minister.....(Interruptions). Part (a) of the question is about the response. I have given you the details of the response. The second part of the question is about the names of leaderso or MPs who have responded. Again, you have put the question and when I give you the names of the MPs which you have asked for, you say my answer is irrelevant. The last part of the question says, `When will you call the meeting?` SHRI CHIMANBHAI MEHTA: That is the most important point. SMT. MARGARET ALVA: It might be, to you. But I am coming by the order. I would like to say one thing to you, through Mr. Chairman, as we have said earlier also-I had said in this House-that we are addressing letters to all the political parties for their comments. After we receive them, we would put them all together and then call a meeting. I only want to say that we have waited. Out of the 49 leaders of the political parties in the two Houses that we had addressed, only five had responded oand out of that, the BJP reply has been that we should leave this to the successor Government and not go into this question at this stage. The Muslim League has written to us saying that they will send us their comments later. Ms Dil Kumari Bhandari is the one who has said that she would want the Prime Minister iand the Chief Ministers included. Mr Chatursnan Mishra has replied and there is a detailed reply from Mr. Chimanbhai Mehta. If the House feels that we should not wait for any responses from the political parties, we are prepared to call a meeting next month or by the end of this month after Parliament adjourns, and have a meeting with the political leaders and get their opinion. But we were waiting for a response from the political leaders. You ask for the permission of the House just now. Yesterday, you had given the warning. MR. CHAIRMAN: She has answered your question. SHRI. CHIMANBHAI MEHTA: No, no. She hasn`t answered. MR: CHAIRMAN: If you wanted a different answer, you should have worded your question differently. SHRI CHAIMANBHAI MEHTA: No, no. She has read out. She said that my question about convening of the meeting was at serial number 3. (Interruptions) MR. CHAIRMAN: Please ask your question. SHRI CHIMANBHAI MEHTA: Whether my question was at serial number 3 or 4, the House has given a consent to you. You know about it, Sir. The Minister should call a meeting. When is she calling a meeting? Kindly give the date. SHRIMATI MARGARET ALVA: Sir, the hon. Member said that I have sent a whole file of papers. We had sent two draft Bills one of which was studied by the Joint Select Committee earlier. As the House is aware, five attempts have been made to work out a consensus by which this Bill can be passed. I have sent you only two Bills-the 1985 Bill which was introduced by the Congress Government and the 1989 Bill which was introduced by the V.P. Singh Government. These were the two Bills which were current and which were studied by the Joint Select Committee. We circulated them and said that we would like to have their comments because there were differences between the two Bills. We have not received them and I was waiting, hoping that some response would come. As I said earlier, certain parties are not interested in immediately pushing it through. As I said earlier we wanted a national debate and we wanted some response. We are prepared to call a meeting of all the political leaders so that a consensus can be worked out. I will not make an announcement about the date today. But immediately after the Session, during the inter-Session period, we are prepared to call a meeting. SHRI CHIMANBHAI MEHTA: If she is prepared to call a meeting, I am satisfied. MR. CHAIRMAN: Shrimati Renuka Chowdhury-not present. (Interruptions) Mr. Surinder Kumar Singla, you cannot raise your hand and stand up by yourself. Please sit down. Shri S.R. Bommai. SHRI SOMAPPA R. BOMMAI: Sir, the Lokpal Bill has been pending for the last many years. It has been discussed by various Committees and it has been debated in the House also. I would like to know whether the Government has a mind to bring in the Lokpal Bill or not. If you have got a mind, then bring it in the next Session. Why do you want to wait for the next Lok Sabha? If you are interested in preventing corruption at the higher levels....(Interruptions).... SHRI M.A. BABY: They want to give you the credit. SHRI SOMAPPA R. BOMMAI: From the date this Government came into existence up till now there have been scandals to the tune of Rs. 1,00,000 crores. The Committees` Reports have come. You don`t want to show the Report on disinvestment. So many reports have come. Don`t you feel the urgency of this Bill? If you don`t feel, say so; otherwise, try to bring it in the next session. SHRIMATI MARGARET ALVA: Sir, I am not passing any opinion on anything. All I am saying is that we have been saying is that in 1989 you introduced a Bill. It was not studied by any committee. It was introduced. There was no need to delay. You did not pass it. You had two years. (Interruptions).... My point is....(Interruptions).... SHRI S. JAIPAL REDDY: We had got only 11 months. SHRI SOMAPPA R. BOMMAI: In 11 months we had brought it. We had introduced it. SHRIMATI MARGARET ALVA: Sir, the Bills have been introduced five times by different Governments including the Government of 1977. The Bills were not passed because you yourselves found that there was no consensus on many parts of the Bill even after they were introduced. My simple point is that if there was a consensus on either the 1989 Bill or the 1985 Bill, let us work it out. We have a draft Bill which I have circulated. You have wanted the draft Bill to be circulated. We have circulated both, the 1985 and the 1989 Bills, and we have asked for your comments. If you send us your comments and point out which of them is acceptable to you, then we can proceed further. But we have not received any comment of any kind. Some parties say, `You wait for the next Parliament to assemble.` Others say, `We will send our comments later.` We must have some response to know on what basis some consensus can be worked out. SYED SIBTEY RAZI: Sir, I submit that the point which I was having in my mind was covered by the hon. Minister. So, there is no need for me to put the question. SHRI S. JAIPAL REDDY: Sir, it is a question of political will on the part of the ruling party. Sir, I had the privilege of serving on the Joint Committee on Lokpal Bill. The Joint Committee had very senior Members from each party including Shri Advani of the BJP. It had five Ministers of the Rajiv Gandhi Government. We went round the country for three years and took evidence from experts and State Governments. When we were concluding our labours, the then Minister of Internal Security, Mr. Chidambaram, made a statement before the Joint Committee on behalf of the Government that the Government did not deem it necessary to institute a Lokpal at all. So, the Government should first make it clear that it wants to bring forward this Bill. I don`t think we need to respond in writing. It is not an academic exercise because I know this to be a political exercise, an exercise in hypocrisy. If you are serious about the Bill, come forward with the Bill. We will make our recommendations and amendments. Will you come forward with any Bill of your kind which brings within its purview the Office of the Prime Minister and the Chief Ministers. SHRIMATI MARGARET ALVA: Sir, I want to make it very clear that in this House the Prime Minister himself has given an assurance and made a commitment...(Interruptions)... SHRI S. JAIPAL REDDY: What is this assurance worth of? SHRIMATI MARGARET ALVA: ...that he will ensure that the office of Prime Minister, the question which you have raised, is brought within the purview of the Bill. (Interruptions)... SHRI CHIMANBHAI MEHTA: But you are not bringing in the Bill. SHRIMATI MARGARET ALVA: We have absolutely no hesitation about it. Sir, Mr. Jaipal Reddy just now said that in 1985 there was a total consensus on some Bill which was before the House. It is strange that in spite of that, in 1989, when they were in power, they brought a new Bill with different perceptions. If they had all agreed on the 1985 Bill, then it could have been reintroduced in 1989.

(Interruptions)... SHRI S. JAIPAL REDDY: No, we did not. We differed in 1985. Your Government at that time did not want to bring the office of Prime Minister within the purview of the Lokpal. That was the bone of contention. SHRIMATI MARGARET ALVA: You had brought it in 1989 in a changed form which you could have immediately passed, if you were serious about it. But, you yourself... (Interruptions)... SHRI S. JAIPAL REDDY: When you were colluding with everybody to depose our Government...(Interruptions)... How could we have got any Bill passed?(Interruptions)... SHRIMATI MARGARET ALVA: Why? (Interruptions)... SHRI S. JAIPAL REDDY: What about you? SHRIMATI MARGARET ALVA: We made a commitment and I stand by it. SHRI DIGVIJAY SINGH: After the elections? SHRIMATI MARGARET ALVA: No. We want to...(Interruptions)... SHRI S. JAIPAL REDDY: What about the Bill? (Interruptions)... SHRIMATI MARGARET ALVA: Sir, we had circulated the two Bills (Interruptions)... SHRI S. JAIPAL REDDY: You introduce the Bill in the House. We shall pass it in one day. (Interruptions)... SHRIMATI MARGARET ALVA: Sir, we want to have a consensus...(Interruptions). SHRI DIGVIJAY SINGH: You introduce the Bill. We will pass the Bill.

(Interruptions)... SHRI S. JAIPAL REDDY: Sir, what is required is will, not the Bill. The question is whether the Government has the will for the Bill. SHRIMATI MARGARET ALVA: Yes, Sir. We have the will for the Bill. We are very keen to get this Bill passed. (Interruptions)... One Minute. Let me finish. If the Members of the House say that they will accept the Bill that the Government introduces, as a consensus, I am prepared to introduce it. If the Members say that they have no suggestions and they will pass the Bill that the Government introduces without the consensus, I accept that (Interruptions)... SHRI INDER KUMAR GUJRAL: Sir, ... MR. CHAIRMAN: Shri Chaturanan Mishra. I cannot call all the Members of one party to put supplementaries. SHRIMATI MARGARET. ALVA: I am sorry, Sir. We have no sin to wash away, whatever they mean by that. I would like to say that we are prepared to take the initiative and since the House wants the Government, without waiting for the replies or the comments, to take the initiative, I shall certainly convey it to the Prime Minister and proceed with it. DR. BIPLAB DASGUPTA: Sir, just to supplement what Shri Jaipal Reddy, said, it appears that the will for the Bill is nil. Sir, the main difference between the 1985 Bill and the 1989 Bill was that the office of the Prime Minister was not brought within the purview of the 1985 Bill. The office of the Prime Minister was brought within the purview of the 1989 Bill. When Minister is saying that the Prime Minister is willing to accept the condition of bringing the office of Prime Minister within the scope, within the jurisdiction of the Lokpal Bill, what stands in the way of bringing this Bill tomorrow? It would require only small amendments here and there. I would like to put the same question. Why should not this Bill be brought in in this Session? What is the problem? All the points have been agreed upon, including bringing the office of Prime Minister within the purview of the Bill. What is the problem? This is my question. SHRIMATI MARGARET ALVA: Sir, this is his opinion which I have noticed. MR. CHAIRMAN: Question No. 63. Shrimati Basanti Sarma. SHRI SURINDER SINGH SINGLA: Sir, I also raised my hand. MR. CHAIRMAN: Not now. That question is over. Now, Question No. 63. SHRIMATI MARGARET ALVA: Sir,... MR. CHAIRMAN: Let me say something. (Interruptions)... I have something to say. The Prime Minister has written to me that-as you know since he is on an official visit to Malaysia, he will not be able answer the questions. He has authorised Shrimati Margaret Alva to answer on his behalf. (Interruptions)... If one person speaks, I will be able to listen to him. SHRI GURUDAS DAS GUPTA: Sir, the point is that there is a Minister of State looking after the office of the Prime Minister. It is understood that the Minister has gone for discharging an international obligation. But what could be the reason for the absence of the Minister of State looking after the Prime Minister`s Office? MR. CHAIRMAN: No, no. He has also written to me...(Interruptions)... SHRI S. JAIPAL REDDY: Sir, why is Mr. Bhuvnesh Chaturvedi absent? SHRI DIGVIJAY SINGH: Yes, Why is Mr. Chaturvedi absent?(Interruptions)... MR. CHAIRMAN: The Minister of State has also written to me and the Prime Minister has talked to me that Mr. Chaturvedi has to sign certain agreements in Malaysia and, therefore, he has to go with him. This has been explained by the Prime Minister to me. SHRI S. JAIPAL REDDY: Mr. Chaturvedi is the shadow of the Prime Minister. He has to go. MR. CHAIRMAN: No. He has some science agreements to sign.(Interruptions)... The Home Minister should reply. Jammu and Kashmir is not an ordinary State. Let the Home Minister reply to it. (Interruptions)... MR. CHAIRMAN: When Mrs. Margaret Alva will reply, I think the Home Minister ...(Interruptions)... SHRI DIGVIJAY SINGH: Sir, I respect Margaret Alvaji`s capability to answer the question. But considering the gravity of the situation, we would request the Home Minister to reply on this issue. (Interruptions)... SHRI S.B. CHAVAN: I think the matter is absolutely clear. The Prime Minister informed the hon. Chairman that he has to go to Malaysia. He also said that Margaret Alvaji will be able to reply to all the questions. If necessary, I would also try to help her. (Interruptions) SHRI GURUDAS DAS GUPTA: What do you mean by helping her? What is wrong in your replying to it? If you reply, heavens will not fall. SHRI DIGVIJAY SINGH: Sir, if he can help her, why can`t he himself reply?

(Interruptions)... SHRI GURUDAS DAS GUPTA: Sir, we want the Question to be deferred. SHRI DIGVIJAY SINGH: Yes, the Question should be deferred. Let only the Prime Minister reply. (Interruptions) SHRI S.B. CHAVAN: Sir, I am prepared to reply. (Interruptions) If the hon. Members want it, I am prepared to reply. (Interruptions) MR. CHAIRMAN: The Home Minister is saying that he is prepared to answer the Question himself. Question No. 63.

records.qtitle: IMPORT OF SUGAR .
records.name: Renuka Chowdhury
records.qn_text:
(a) what would be the total cost of import of five lakh tonnes of sugar including customs and other relevant charges

(b) what is the current international price of one tonne sugar and the difference between prices of sugar import and current international price

(c) whether Government are thinking to scrap the sugar import contract; and

(d) if so, what would be the loss?
records.ans_text:
:- THE MINISTER OF FOOD (SHRI AJIT SINGH)

(a) As per information received from the State Trading Corporation of India Ltd. and the Minerals and Metals Trading Corporation of India Ltd. the total contracted quantity of imported sugar as on date held by them stands at 2.91 lakh tonnes with the total value of about US $1231.62 lakhs. The customs and other relevant charges thereon would be known if and when actual import of sugar takes place.

(b) The London Daily price (LDP) of one tonne sugar on 26-7-95 was US $ 466.50 Fob. (Free on board). STC and MMTC have indicated that the weighted average of contract price of 2.91 lakh tonnes of imported sugar is US $ 423.24 PMT. C & FFO

(which includes freight charges upto nearest Indian Port). However, these two figures are not comparable as the freight charges are not included in the LDP which varies on the place of origin sugar.

(c) and (d) In view of comfortable position of sugar production in our country,in the current season in our Government decided in June,1995 to dispose of contracted (imported) sugar at best possible international price. Out of the initially contracted quantity of about 4.09 lakh tonnes, STC and MMTC have been able to reduce the contracted quantity to 2.91 lakh by sweeping off/cancellation of the 1.18 lakh tonnes out of the total contracted quantity. The loss/gain, if any, would be known only after completion of the transactions. SHRIMATI RENUKA CHOWDHURY : I disagree with it ...(interruptions) ... It is a very bureaucratic presumption of what has happened in the country. A few month ago, we did not anticipate the shortfall in the sugar production in the country. That had resulted in the sugar scam. Today, ...(Interruptions)... Part (a) of my question is why did they fail to take that question into consideration? ...(Interruptions)... SHRIMATI RENUKA CHOWDHURY : That is part (a) of my question. SHRIMATI RENUKA CHOWDHURY : If we have to pay any cancellation charges ...(interruptions)... That is part (a) of my question, Sir. ...(interruptions)... MR. CHAIRMAN : Please sit down, all of you. Please hear him. ...(interruptions)... Don`t you want to heare him? ANSWER:- THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HOME AFFAIRS (SHRI P. M. SAYEED): Sir, regarding the Naina Sahni case, the charge-sheet has already been filed in sub judice. We will not be in a position. ...(interruptions)... MR. CHAIRMAN: Will you allow us to proceed? ...(interruptions)... I adjourn the House up to twelve o`clock. The House then adjourned at thirty-two minutes past eleven of the clock and reassembled at one minute past twelve of the clock, THE DEPUTY CHAIRMAN In the Chair.
